{"id":"e0607ce5-7d2f-48bd-ab0b-0242c445dfc7","title":"Architecture & Delivery Plan — SFN-20: Build mdfn as the Superfunctions Markdown authoring platform","content":"Backlog issue: [SFN-20 — Build mdfn as the Superfunctions Markdown authoring platform](<https://linear.app/21n/issue/SFN-20/build-mdfn-as-the-superfunctions-markdown-authoring-platform>)

## Architecture objective

Deliver a modular Markdown platform whose core semantics are independent of UI framework, storage, transport, collaboration provider, and product surface.

The architecture must support a progression from parser/serializer use to visual editing and optional collaborative services without replacing the durable Markdown contract.

## Non-negotiable architecture rules

 1. Markdown source is always present in the durable snapshot.
 2. Runtime structured state is versioned, derived, and invalidated by schema/source identity.
 3. Unsupported constructs survive as opaque, diagnosable content.
 4. Core commands and transactions cannot import DOM, UI, framework, server, or product packages.
 5. Framework adapters bind shared behavior and cannot fork it.
 6. UIFn owns editor chrome; mdfn owns editing semantics.
 7. Optional server packages use shared HTTP, database, authentication, and file abstractions.
 8. Database adapters are wrapped internally with the mdfn schema.
 9. Raw HTML is disabled by default and every rendering/import boundary has a security policy.
10. Extension behavior is defined once and validated by conformance suites.

## Layered system

```text
Markdown source and sidecar metadata
                ↓
@mdfn/markdown: parse, serialize, format, diagnose, source map
                ↓
@mdfn/core: schema, document, transactions, commands, history, extensions
                ↓
@mdfn/dom + @mdfn/source: browser editing and source editing
                ↓
@mdfn/adapter-kit
       ↙             ↓             ↘
@mdfn/react     @mdfn/svelte    @mdfn/solid
       ↘             ↓             ↙
@mdfn/components + framework component bindings + UIFn
                ↓
optional collab, server, files, content, search, AI bridges
```

Rendering can consume the Markdown pipeline directly or project structured documents into safe HTML without loading browser editing packages.

## Proposed package graph

### Stable foundation

* `@mdfn/core` — schema, nodes, marks, selections, steps, transactions, commands, history, extension registry, versioning, migrations
* `@mdfn/markdown` — CommonMark/GFM pipeline, positional AST, source spans, parsing, serialization, formatting, diagnostics, preservation metadata
* `@mdfn/render` — safe HTML and render-tree output, sanitization hooks, read-only render policies
* `@mdfn/dom` — DOM editor view, events, selection bridge, clipboard, drag/drop, composition, input handling, node views
* `@mdfn/source` — source editor state, syntax highlighting integration, source diagnostics, source/visual synchronization
* `@mdfn/extensions` — supported extension packs exposed through subpath exports
* `@mdfn/adapter-kit` — lifecycle, subscription, action, and renderer contracts shared by framework bindings
* `@mdfn/react`
* `@mdfn/svelte`
* `@mdfn/solid`
* `@mdfn/components` — framework-neutral component recipes and editor UI contracts
* `@mdfn/components-react`
* `@mdfn/components-svelte`
* `@mdfn/components-solid`
* `@mdfn/testing` — corpus, traces, fixtures, harnesses, extension certification
* `@mdfn/registry` — optional registry metadata and installation composition
* `mdfn` — curated facade for common use cases

### Optional platform packages

* `@mdfn/collab` — provider-neutral collaborative state, awareness, comments, suggestions, history contracts
* `@mdfn/client` — client for self-hosted document and collaboration services
* `@mdfn/server` — HTTP routes, persistence services, authorization hooks, migrations
* `@mdfn/filefn` — FileFn asset-provider bridge
* `@mdfn/contentfn` — explicit Markdown content-type bridge
* `@mdfn/searchfn` — indexing and extraction bridge
* `@mdfn/ai` — provider-neutral assistant actions expressed as reviewable transactions or suggestions

Extension packs should use subpath exports rather than one workspace package per node or mark.

## Dependency policy

Allowed dependencies flow downward only:

* Markdown may depend on core types that are environment-neutral.
* Render may depend on core and Markdown.
* DOM and source may depend on core, Markdown, and render.
* Adapter kit may depend on environment-neutral core APIs.
* Framework packages may depend on adapter kit and browser layers.
* Components may depend on core contracts and UIFn recipes, with framework component packages depending on their matching adapters.
* Optional integrations may depend on stable foundation packages and the relevant Superfunctions package.
* Core must never import DOM, framework, UIFn, product integration, collaboration, or server packages.

A repository verifier must fail forbidden edges, framework cross-imports, private deep imports, circular dependencies, missing package metadata, or public exports that bypass the declared graph.

## Document and snapshot model

```ts
interface MdfnSnapshot {
  format: "mdfn";
  version: 1;
  markdown: string;
  document?: MdfnJSON;
  schemaHash: string;
  sourceHash: string;
  diagnostics: Diagnostic[];
  sidecar?: MdfnSidecar;
}

interface MdfnSidecar {
  comments?: CommentThread[];
  suggestions?: Suggestion[];
  assets?: AssetMetadata[];
  historyRef?: string;
}

interface MdfnJSON {
  type: "doc";
  schemaVersion: number;
  attrs?: Record<string, unknown>;
  content: MdfnNode[];
}

interface MdfnNode {
  type: string;
  attrs?: Record<string, unknown>;
  marks?: MdfnMark[];
  content?: MdfnNode[];
  text?: string;
  source?: {
    from: number;
    to: number;
    raw?: string;
    syntax?: Record<string, unknown>;
    preservation: "exact" | "semantic" | "opaque";
  };
}
```

Stable node identifiers are required where comments, suggestions, collaborative anchors, or external references need identity. Identifiers must not leak into portable Markdown unless a syntax extension explicitly owns them.

## Parse, edit, and serialize pipeline

 1. Detect dialect, extension configuration, encoding, and line endings.
 2. Parse to a positional Markdown AST with raw slices for relevant constructs.
 3. Resolve syntax through the enabled extension registry.
 4. Convert supported nodes into the runtime document.
 5. Preserve unsupported or disabled syntax as opaque nodes with diagnostics.
 6. Record source spans and formatting metadata needed by the declared preservation level.
 7. Apply edits through transactions and schema validation.
 8. Track dirty spans and structural dependencies.
 9. Serialize unchanged regions from source slices when exact preservation applies.
10. Serialize edited regions through extension serializers.
11. Format only when explicitly requested or when an edit requires local normalization.
12. Emit diagnostics for lossy conversions, unsupported constructs, invalid nesting, security policy decisions, and migration needs.

## Core transaction contract

The core engine needs:

* Immutable or persistence-friendly document state
* Selections and positions
* Atomic steps and invertible transactions
* Command dispatch and command capability checks
* History grouping and undo/redo
* Schema validation
* Plugin state
* Append/filter transaction hooks
* Mapping positions through edits
* Deterministic JSON serialization
* Extension-controlled migrations
* Diagnostic accumulation
* Stable semantic traces for testing

Consumers should receive explicit change objects including document changes, selection changes, changed source spans, diagnostics, and sidecar anchor mappings.

## Extension SDK

Each extension may contribute:

```ts
interface MdfnExtension {
  name: string;
  version: string;
  priority?: number;
  schema?: SchemaContribution;
  parseMarkdown?: MarkdownParseRules;
  serializeMarkdown?: MarkdownSerializeRules;
  render?: RenderRules;
  sanitize?: SecurityPolicyContribution;
  commands?: CommandMap;
  keymap?: KeyBinding[];
  inputRules?: InputRule[];
  pasteRules?: PasteRule[];
  plugins?: CorePlugin[];
  migrations?: SchemaMigration[];
  domRenderers?: Record<string, DomRenderer>;
  diagnostics?: DiagnosticRule[];
  tests?: ExtensionConformanceManifest;
  preservation?: PreservationDeclaration;
}
```

Extensions must declare syntax ownership, conflicts, dependencies, preservation behavior, security behavior, and migration compatibility. The registry rejects incompatible extension graphs before editor creation.

## Dialect and extension strategy

* Baseline: CommonMark
* Default: GFM
* Candidate extension packs: frontmatter, footnotes, math, callouts, directives, diagrams, custom fenced blocks, mentions, assets
* Raw HTML: opt-in policy extension, disabled by default
* Executable mixed-framework syntax: separate opt-in family with isolated parsing, rendering, and security contracts

Each extension requires parser, serializer, renderer, diagnostics, migration, unknown-syntax, security, and round-trip fixtures.

## Browser editing layer

The DOM layer is responsible for:

* Browser selection synchronization
* Before-input and input handling
* Composition and IME safety
* Clipboard import/export
* Drag/drop
* Focus and blur
* DOM mutation reconciliation
* Node views and decorators
* Scrolling and coordinate mapping
* Accessibility semantics
* Mobile behavior
* Browser-specific compatibility

Browser primitives should come from a proven structured-editing kernel. mdfn owns the surrounding contracts, Markdown fidelity, extensions, tests, and public API.

## Source editing and mode synchronization

Source mode should use a dedicated source-editor engine behind `@mdfn/source`. The integration must:

* Share the same Markdown diagnostics and extension registry
* Map selections between source and structured views where possible
* Preserve scroll and active heading context
* Debounce parsing without losing deterministic state
* Surface syntax errors without destroying the last valid structured state
* Define whether split mode updates continuously or transactionally
* Handle edits that cannot be represented by the active structured schema
* Keep undo behavior intelligible when switching modes

The source is authoritative at persistence boundaries. Visual edits update source through the preservation-aware serializer.

## Framework contract

The vanilla DOM API is the browser reference surface. Framework adapters provide:

* Editor lifecycle creation and disposal
* Fine-grained state subscriptions
* Stable action and command bindings
* Node-view rendering bridges
* Portal/overlay integration
* SSR-safe imports and hydration boundaries
* Framework-native context and composition APIs

They must not implement unique command logic, normalization, parsing, serialization, schema, or persistence behavior.

A shared semantic trace describes inputs and expected transactions, document output, selection, diagnostics, and emitted events. The same trace runs against vanilla DOM, React, Svelte, and Solid.

## UIFn integration

mdfn components should consume UIFn foundations for:

* Buttons and toggles
* Tooltips
* Menus and command palettes
* Dialogs and popovers
* Focus scopes and roving focus
* Tabs and mode switching
* Forms and comboboxes
* Theming and tokens
* Responsive layout
* Screen-reader semantics

UIFn components dispatch mdfn commands and read mdfn state. They never mutate document structure directly.

## Rendering and security

The render pipeline must support browser and server output with:

* Escaping by default
* URL protocol allowlists
* Link target and rel policies
* Raw HTML gating and sanitization
* Image and asset policies
* Embed allowlists and sandbox attributes
* Extension-specific sanitizers
* Maximum nesting, node, token, and input-size limits
* Time and memory budgets
* Safe diagnostic output
* Trusted-types compatibility where applicable

Pasted HTML follows a separate import policy and is normalized through schema-aware rules. It must never bypass render sanitization.

Security verification includes malicious Markdown corpora, unsafe URLs, malformed Unicode, deep nesting, large tokens, parser differentials, paste payloads, embed policies, authorization checks, and fuzzing.

## Collaboration architecture

The collaboration package wraps a proven shared-document engine behind mdfn contracts:

* Document update encoding
* Awareness and presence
* Selection anchors
* Offline queueing and reconnect
* Snapshot compaction
* Schema version negotiation
* Migration coordination
* Comment and suggestion anchors
* Authorization callbacks
* Audit events

The core remains usable without collaboration dependencies. Comments and suggestions live in sidecar state and map through document transactions. Conflict-safe migration requires a protocol that prevents incompatible clients from editing the same document version.

## Server architecture

`@mdfn/server` should expose services and transport-neutral handlers for:

* Document create/read/update/version operations
* Snapshot and update persistence
* Collaboration sessions
* Comment and suggestion workflows
* Asset authorization and metadata
* History and restore
* Schema/version negotiation
* Health and diagnostics

HTTP adapters remain consumer-selected. The package uses shared HTTP router contracts and does not re-export framework adapters.

Incoming shared database adapters are wrapped internally:

```ts
const database = wrapWithSchema(config.database, getMdfnSchema(config));
```

Consumers should not have to pass an mdfn schema into shared database adapter constructors.

## Superfunctions integration contracts

### DocsFn adoption

* Replace duplicated Markdown interpretation with `@mdfn/markdown`.
* Supply a DocsFn extension bundle.
* Project the canonical AST/document into current DocsFn blocks during migration.
* Run compatibility fixtures before switching defaults.
* Preserve existing rendering output or document intentional migrations.

### ContentFn adoption

* Add an explicit Markdown content type and version.
* Preserve current rich-text blocks as a separate format.
* Provide opt-in conversions with diagnostics for loss.
* Store extension and raw-HTML policies with content metadata.

### CmsFn adoption

* Compose mdfn editor components in its authoring application.
* Persist through explicit ContentFn Markdown values or mdfn snapshots.
* Supply migration tooling and previews for existing rich text.

### FileFn adoption

Define an asset provider:

```ts
interface MdfnAssetProvider {
  select?(context: AssetContext): Promise<AssetReference>;
  upload?(file: File, context: AssetContext): Promise<AssetReference>;
  resolve(reference: AssetReference): Promise<ResolvedAsset>;
  authorize?(operation: AssetOperation, reference: AssetReference): Promise<void>;
}
```

Source should prefer durable identifiers or stable references; renderers resolve delivery URLs.

### SearchFn adoption

Expose deterministic extraction:

* `extractPlainText`
* `extractHeadings`
* `extractLinks`
* `extractChunks`
* `extractMetadata`

All functions accept the same dialect and extension configuration as the editor.

## Delivery phases

### Phase 0 — Contracts and risk spikes

Deliver:

* Product scope and non-goals
* Source-preservation specification
* Runtime document and snapshot specification
* Package DAG and dependency rules
* Extension SDK contract
* Dialect and security policy
* Framework parity contract
* Editing-kernel and source-editor evaluation
* Collaboration-engine evaluation
* Representative syntax and browser risk prototypes

Exit criteria:

* Exact, semantic, and opaque preservation behaviors pass representative fixtures.
* Unknown syntax survives a no-edit cycle.
* Transactions can map source spans.
* One custom extension parses, edits, serializes, renders, diagnoses, and migrates.
* Vanilla DOM plus one framework spike demonstrates shared semantics.
* Licensing, bundle, SSR, IME, mobile, and browser constraints are understood.

### Phase 1 — Headless foundation

Deliver:

* `@mdfn/core`
* `@mdfn/markdown`
* `@mdfn/render`
* Initial extension packs
* Snapshot and migration model
* Diagnostics and formatter
* Headless testing package
* Safe read-only rendering

Exit criteria:

* CommonMark/GFM corpus gates pass.
* Supported syntax meets semantic round-trip thresholds.
* No-edit fixtures meet exact-preservation targets.
* Unknown constructs remain opaque with diagnostics.
* Security corpus and parser fuzz harness are active.
* Packages work in isolated packed consumers.

### Phase 2 — Browser editing

Deliver:

* `@mdfn/dom`
* `@mdfn/source`
* Visual, source, split, preview, and read-only modes
* History, commands, selection, clipboard, drag/drop, composition
* Essential node views
* Browser and mobile harnesses

Exit criteria:

* Editing semantics pass Chrome, Firefox, and Safari matrices.
* IME/composition suites cover representative input methods.
* Clipboard fixtures cover internal, Markdown, HTML, office-like, and plain-text sources.
* Source/visual switching preserves document and selection expectations.
* Keystroke, parse, and memory budgets pass representative large documents.
* SSR imports are side-effect safe.

### Phase 3 — Framework adapters and UI

Deliver:

* Adapter kit
* React, Svelte, and Solid packages
* Headless and styled editor components
* UIFn-based toolbar, bubble controls, command palette, links, tables, files, outline, diagnostics
* Registry composition
* Framework examples and packed consumers

Exit criteria:

* Every semantic trace passes for vanilla DOM, React, Svelte, and Solid.
* No framework package owns unique editor semantics.
* Accessibility checks cover keyboard navigation, screen readers, focus, dialogs, and high contrast.
* SSR/hydration examples pass for supported framework environments.
* Package graph verifier passes with zero forbidden edges.

### Phase 4 — Ecosystem adoption

Deliver:

* DocsFn canonical parser integration and compatibility projection
* Explicit ContentFn Markdown type
* CmsFn authoring integration
* FileFn asset provider
* SearchFn extraction bridge
* Migration and compatibility tooling

Exit criteria:

* Existing DocsFn fixtures pass or have approved documented migrations.
* ContentFn storage remains explicit and versioned.
* CmsFn can author, preview, save, reload, and migrate Markdown content.
* File references survive save/reload and authorization changes.
* Search output matches canonical document interpretation.
* Downstream packages consume public APIs only.

### Phase 5 — Collaboration and editorial platform

Deliver:

* Collaboration provider contracts and implementation
* Client/server packages
* Presence and offline synchronization
* Comments, suggestions, review state, and history
* AuthFn/HTTP/database integrations
* Operational diagnostics and compaction

Exit criteria:

* Concurrent and offline edit simulations converge.
* Anchors survive representative edits and migrations.
* Incompatible schemas are negotiated or rejected safely.
* Authorization and audit tests cover document, comment, suggestion, asset, and history operations.
* Persistence recovery and compaction tests pass.
* Multi-user performance budgets pass.

## Verification matrix

### Parser and serializer

* CommonMark corpus
* GFM corpus
* Extension fixtures
* No-edit byte identity
* Semantic round trips
* Touched-region normalization
* Unknown and disabled syntax
* Line endings and Unicode
* Malformed and adversarial input
* Migration chains

### Core engine

* Transaction invertibility
* Position mapping
* Selection mapping
* History grouping
* Command availability
* Plugin isolation
* Schema validation
* Diagnostics
* Deterministic snapshots
* Sidecar anchor mapping

### Browser

* Chrome, Firefox, Safari
* Desktop and mobile viewports
* Keyboard-only operation
* IME and composition
* Screen readers
* Clipboard sources
* Drag/drop
* Focus and overlays
* Large documents
* DOM mutation recovery

### Frameworks

* Vanilla reference traces
* React traces and SSR
* Svelte traces and SSR
* Solid traces and SSR
* Node-view lifecycle
* Subscription cleanup
* Hydration boundaries
* Framework package isolation

### Security

* Raw HTML policy
* URL sanitization
* Paste sanitization
* Embed sandboxing
* Asset authorization
* Resource exhaustion
* Fuzzing
* Collaboration authorization
* Snapshot validation
* Extension policy conflicts

### Packaging

* ESM consumers
* CommonJS consumers where promised
* Type declarations
* Tree shaking
* Side-effect declarations
* Browser/server entry separation
* Export maps
* Packed installs
* Workspace-boundary verifier
* Minimum supported runtimes

## Performance budgets to define in Phase 0

Set explicit budgets for:

* Initial parse by document size
* Incremental edit and keystroke latency
* Markdown serialization latency
* Source/visual mode switch latency
* Memory by document size
* DOM nodes and viewport rendering
* Clipboard import latency
* Collaboration update size and fan-out
* Snapshot load and compaction
* Server render throughput

Budgets should be validated on representative documents, lower-powered devices, and all supported browsers.

## Repository placement

Create mdfn as a top-level multi-package function inside the root monorepo, not a nested monorepo.

Recommended planning bundle:

```text
mdfn/
  .conduct/
    MDFN-01/
      product.md
      content-model.md
      architecture.md
      extension-sdk.md
      security.md
      verification.md
      phases.md
```

Published function packages follow the multi-package form `@mdfn/<package>`, with the curated facade published as `mdfn`. Shared ecosystem-independent primitives belong in `packages/` only if multiple functions genuinely own the abstraction.

## Engineering effort and team shape

Engineering-effort bands:

* Contracts and risk spikes: **4–6 engineer-weeks**
* Integrated prototype: **8–12 engineer-weeks**
* Production headless/browser foundation: **9–15 engineer-months**
* Complete self-hosted platform: **18–30 engineer-months**

A practical team shape includes:

* Editing/browser architecture ownership
* Markdown/parser and source-fidelity ownership
* Cross-framework and UIFn ownership
* Collaboration/backend ownership when Phase 5 begins
* Dedicated accessibility and security review capacity

Do not convert these bands into calendar commitments until Phase 0 closes the kernel, preservation, syntax, browser, and collaboration risks.

## Immediate next decision

Before implementation, approve or revise:

 1. The three-level preservation contract
 2. CommonMark baseline and GFM default
 3. Stable versus optional package boundary
 4. Extension SDK responsibilities
 5. Framework parity contract
 6. Raw HTML and embed security defaults
 7. First stable release boundary
 8. DocsFn compatibility approach

## Decision summary

Build mdfn as a **Markdown-native, framework-neutral authoring platform** for the Superfunctions ecosystem.

mdfn should not be a single editor component or a renderer-only package. It should provide:

* A headless document, transaction, command, and extension layer
* A first-class Markdown parser, serializer, formatter, and diagnostics pipeline
* A vanilla DOM integration surface
* Equal adapters for React, Svelte, and Solid
* Composable editor UI built from UIFn
* Optional self-hosted collaboration, comments, suggestions, history, persistence, assets, and AI capabilities
* Explicit integrations for DocsFn, ContentFn, CmsFn, FileFn, SearchFn, AuthFn, and shared HTTP/database abstractions

The durable portable format is Markdown source. A structured runtime document model may power editing, but it must not become an undocumented replacement for the source contract.

## Product opportunity

Superfunctions already has adjacent capabilities:

* **DocsFn** compiles Markdown into renderable content blocks.
* **ContentFn** models portable structured content.
* **CmsFn** has authoring surfaces but no complete rich editing engine.
* **UIFn** provides a mature cross-framework UI architecture.
* **FileFn** can own durable assets and delivery.
* **SearchFn** can index normalized text, headings, and document chunks.
* **AuthFn**, shared HTTP packages, and shared database packages can support self-hosted multi-user services.

The missing layer is a shared authoring substrate. Today, products that need Markdown editing would otherwise need to independently solve selection, history, keyboard behavior, clipboard import, source mode, parser/serializer fidelity, UI behavior, extensions, framework bindings, persistence, collaboration, security, and migrations.

mdfn turns those recurring costs into a reusable function and creates a single compatibility surface between editing, documentation, CMS, content, file, search, and application workflows.

## Product thesis

The strongest product is one where:

1. Markdown remains inspectable, portable, version-control-friendly, and durable.
2. Visual editing is powerful without making source fidelity accidental.
3. Framework adapters are bindings over one shared semantic engine.
4. UI chrome composes through UIFn but editing semantics do not depend on UIFn.
5. Self-hosted services are optional and use existing Superfunctions abstractions.
6. Unsupported syntax is preserved with diagnostics, never silently deleted.
7. Teams can begin with a headless editor and add collaboration or product integrations without changing the core document contract.

## Primary users and jobs

### Application developers

* Embed a polished Markdown editor without accepting a framework lock-in.
* Add custom syntax, commands, node views, toolbar controls, and persistence.
* Use the same document behavior in multiple frontend stacks.
* Render the same source safely on servers, browsers, and documentation sites.

### Documentation teams

* Author CommonMark/GFM content visually or in source mode.
* Use frontmatter, code, tables, task lists, footnotes, math, callouts, diagrams, and custom directives.
* Keep source suitable for repositories and build pipelines.
* Preview exactly what will be published.

### Product and CMS teams

* Store Markdown as an explicit content type.
* Attach assets through FileFn without leaking temporary URLs into source.
* Add comments, suggestions, approvals, and history.
* Index content and headings through SearchFn.

### Platform maintainers

* Enforce one parser/serializer contract across products.
* Add extensions without forking core behavior.
* Migrate schemas and syntax versions safely.
* Test framework parity and security centrally.

## Product principles

### Markdown is the durable boundary

The persisted contract should always include Markdown. Runtime JSON may be cached or stored for performance, collaboration, or diagnostics, but it must be versioned and reproducible from the source contract.

### Preservation is explicit

The product must distinguish three guarantees:

1. **No-edit preservation:** importing and exporting without an edit returns byte-identical source.
2. **Semantic round trip:** supported syntax returns equivalent Markdown even when formatting normalizes.
3. **Touched-region normalization:** editing one region does not rewrite unrelated source.

Each extension declares its preservation behavior. Source spans, syntax metadata, raw slices, opaque nodes, and diagnostics must support these guarantees.

### One semantic engine, multiple bindings

Core commands, transactions, selection semantics, validation, and extension behavior live outside framework packages. React, Svelte, and Solid adapters bind lifecycle and rendering only. A semantic trace suite runs against every adapter.

### Progressive capability

Consumers should be able to choose:

* Headless parsing and transformation
* Read-only rendering
* Source editing
* Visual editing
* Split editing and preview
* Composable editor chrome
* Assets and embeds
* Persistence
* Collaboration and editorial workflows

Optional layers must not inflate or constrain the core.

### Secure defaults

Raw HTML is disabled by default. Links, pasted HTML, custom embeds, assets, and server operations use explicit policies. Parsing and rendering must defend against unsafe URLs, script injection, malformed input, and resource-exhaustion attacks.

## Product surface

### Foundational editing

* Paragraphs, headings, block quotes, thematic breaks
* Bold, italic, strike, inline code, links
* Ordered, unordered, nested, and task lists
* Code blocks with language metadata
* Tables and alignment
* Images, files, and embeds
* Selection-aware commands and keyboard shortcuts
* Undo/redo and transaction history
* Drag/drop and clipboard import
* Placeholder, read-only, and disabled states
* Markdown, HTML, JSON, and plain-text import/export

### Markdown-native authoring

* CommonMark baseline and GFM default
* Frontmatter
* Footnotes
* Math
* Callouts and directives
* Diagram and custom fenced blocks
* Reference links and definitions
* Custom components through an opt-in portable directive contract
* Formatting and diagnostics
* Source, visual, split, preview, and read-only modes
* Source-preservation reporting

Executable mixed-framework syntax should remain a separate opt-in extension family because it weakens portability, security, and renderer independence.

### Editor UI

* Fixed and floating toolbars
* Bubble controls
* Slash-command palette
* Link editor
* Table controls
* File and embed dialogs
* Outline and heading navigation
* Diagnostics panel
* Comments and suggestion surfaces
* Version/history interface
* Responsive and mobile toolbar patterns

UIFn should own visual components, focus management, overlays, themes, and accessibility primitives. mdfn should own editor state and semantic actions.

### Collaboration and editorial workflows

* Realtime document synchronization
* Offline edits and reconnect
* Presence and selections
* Threaded comments
* Suggestions and review state
* Version history
* Schema-aware migration
* Authorization and audit hooks

These capabilities should use a proven collaborative data engine behind mdfn-owned interfaces. The project should not invent merge algorithms from first principles.

## Ecosystem fit

### UIFn

Use UIFn for editor chrome and accessibility primitives. Reuse its package layering:

core → DOM → adapter kit → framework adapters → components/style → registry

mdfn must add stronger semantic parity tests so framework packages cannot fork editing behavior.

### DocsFn

DocsFn should consume the canonical mdfn Markdown pipeline through a docs-specific extension set and a compatibility projection to its rendering model. Existing behavior should migrate incrementally, not through a flag day.

### ContentFn

Add an explicit Markdown content value rather than silently reinterpreting rich-text blocks:

```ts
type MarkdownContent = {
  kind: "markdown";
  source: string;
  dialect: "commonmark" | "gfm";
  extensions: string[];
  allowRawHtml: boolean;
  schemaVersion: number;
};
```

### CmsFn

CmsFn authoring can compose mdfn framework components, while stored content remains framework-independent. Existing rich-text data needs explicit migration and compatibility rules.

### FileFn

Integrate through an asset-provider interface. Markdown stores durable asset identifiers or stable references with fallback URLs and metadata; upload orchestration remains in FileFn.

### SearchFn

Expose deterministic helpers for plain text, headings, links, and chunks so search indexing derives from the same document interpretation used by editing and rendering.

### AuthFn, HTTP, and database packages

Optional mdfn server packages should accept shared HTTP and database contracts. Any incoming database adapter must be wrapped internally with mdfn's schema before use. Authentication and authorization should integrate through hooks and middleware rather than hard-coded providers.

## Source and persistence contract

A persisted snapshot can follow this shape:

```ts
interface MdfnSnapshot {
  format: "mdfn";
  version: 1;
  markdown: string;
  document?: MdfnJSON;
  schemaHash: string;
  diagnostics: Diagnostic[];
  sidecar?: {
    comments?: CommentThread[];
    suggestions?: Suggestion[];
    assetMetadata?: AssetMetadata[];
  };
}
```

The structured document cache is valid only when its schema hash and source identity match. Comments and suggestions live in a sidecar because they are editorial state, not portable Markdown syntax.

## Differentiation

mdfn's durable advantage is the combination of:

* Markdown-first source guarantees
* Framework-neutral semantics
* Equal multi-framework adapters
* Self-hostable optional services
* Extensible syntax and node behavior
* Explicit compatibility with the rest of Superfunctions
* Inspectable security and migration contracts
* A path from headless parsing to collaborative authoring without replacing the document model

## Success measures

Product success should be measured through verifiable outcomes:

* No-edit and supported-syntax round-trip corpus pass rates
* Unknown-syntax preservation rate
* Cross-framework semantic trace parity
* Keystroke and parse latency budgets
* Browser, mobile, IME, clipboard, SSR, and accessibility conformance
* Security corpus and fuzz-test results
* Packed-consumer success across supported module formats
* Successful DocsFn compatibility projection
* Successful ContentFn and CmsFn Markdown-type adoption
* FileFn asset and SearchFn extraction interoperability
* Number of downstream products using the shared engine without forks

## Scope controls

The first stable foundation should prioritize:

* Content and preservation contracts
* Headless transactions, commands, extensions, parsing, serialization, rendering, and diagnostics
* Browser editing primitives and source mode
* Vanilla DOM plus framework parity
* Essential editor UI
* Security, packaging, performance, and migration gates

Collaboration, comments, suggestions, history, AI, and full server persistence should remain optional packages and may advance after the foundation proves the document and extension contracts.

## Key product risks

* Choosing preservation semantics after coding begins
* Allowing runtime JSON to become the undocumented canonical format
* Adapter-specific command or selection logic
* Excessive stable package count
* Silent loss of unsupported syntax
* Unsafe HTML, links, embeds, or pasted content
* Treating browser, mobile, IME, clipboard, and SSR behavior as late polish
* Coupling optional collaboration or persistence into the core
* Forcing ecosystem adoption before compatibility projections and migrations exist

## Open product decisions

* Mandatory preservation level for the first stable release
* Default extension set beyond CommonMark and GFM
* Whether frontmatter, footnotes, math, directives, and diagrams are default or opt-in
* First-release boundary between browser foundation and collaboration
* Stable public facade versus advanced direct imports
* Initial performance and bundle budgets
* Versioning policy for syntax, schema, snapshots, and sidecars
* Migration requirements for existing content stores
* Whether source maps and diagnostics are exposed as a stable public API

## Rough effort model

These are engineering-effort bands for backlog shaping, not delivery dates:

* Architecture contracts and risk spikes: **4–6 engineer-weeks**
* Integrated prototype: **8–12 engineer-weeks**
* Production headless and browser foundation: **9–15 engineer-months**
* Complete self-hosted authoring platform: **18–30 engineer-months**

The production scope is best handled by a small cross-functional team with deep editing/browser expertise, framework integration experience, and dedicated security and accessibility review.

## Recommendation

Proceed through contract-first risk reduction. Approve the product thesis, preservation guarantees, package boundaries, extension contract, and ecosystem compatibility strategy before selecting final implementation dependencies or building broad UI. ## Architecture objective

Deliver a modular Markdown platform whose core semantics are independent of UI framework, storage, transport, collaboration provider, and product surface.

The architecture must support a progression from parser/serializer use to visual editing and optional collaborative services without replacing the durable Markdown contract.

## Non-negotiable architecture rules

 1. Markdown source is always present in the durable snapshot.
 2. Runtime structured state is versioned, derived, and invalidated by schema/source identity.
 3. Unsupported constructs survive as opaque, diagnosable content.
 4. Core commands and transactions cannot import DOM, UI, framework, server, or product packages.
 5. Framework adapters bind shared behavior and cannot fork it.
 6. UIFn owns editor chrome; mdfn owns editing semantics.
 7. Optional server packages use shared HTTP, database, authentication, and file abstractions.
 8. Database adapters are wrapped internally with the mdfn schema.
 9. Raw HTML is disabled by default and every rendering/import boundary has a security policy.
10. Extension behavior is defined once and validated by conformance suites.

## Layered system

```text
Markdown source and sidecar metadata
                ↓
@mdfn/markdown: parse, serialize, format, diagnose, source map
                ↓
@mdfn/core: schema, document, transactions, commands, history, extensions
                ↓
@mdfn/dom + @mdfn/source: browser editing and source editing
                ↓
@mdfn/adapter-kit
       ↙             ↓             ↘
@mdfn/react     @mdfn/svelte    @mdfn/solid
       ↘             ↓             ↙
@mdfn/components + framework component bindings + UIFn
                ↓
optional collab, server, files, content, search, AI bridges
```

Rendering can consume the Markdown pipeline directly or project structured documents into safe HTML without loading browser editing packages.

## Proposed package graph

### Stable foundation

* `@mdfn/core` — schema, nodes, marks, selections, steps, transactions, commands, history, extension registry, versioning, migrations
* `@mdfn/markdown` — CommonMark/GFM pipeline, positional AST, source spans, parsing, serialization, formatting, diagnostics, preservation metadata
* `@mdfn/render` — safe HTML and render-tree output, sanitization hooks, read-only render policies
* `@mdfn/dom` — DOM editor view, events, selection bridge, clipboard, drag/drop, composition, input handling, node views
* `@mdfn/source` — source editor state, syntax highlighting integration, source diagnostics, source/visual synchronization
* `@mdfn/extensions` — supported extension packs exposed through subpath exports
* `@mdfn/adapter-kit` — lifecycle, subscription, action, and renderer contracts shared by framework bindings
* `@mdfn/react`
* `@mdfn/svelte`
* `@mdfn/solid`
* `@mdfn/components` — framework-neutral component recipes and editor UI contracts
* `@mdfn/components-react`
* `@mdfn/components-svelte`
* `@mdfn/components-solid`
* `@mdfn/testing` — corpus, traces, fixtures, harnesses, extension certification
* `@mdfn/registry` — optional registry metadata and installation composition
* `mdfn` — curated facade for common use cases

### Optional platform packages

* `@mdfn/collab` — provider-neutral collaborative state, awareness, comments, suggestions, history contracts
* `@mdfn/client` — client for self-hosted document and collaboration services
* `@mdfn/server` — HTTP routes, persistence services, authorization hooks, migrations
* `@mdfn/filefn` — FileFn asset-provider bridge
* `@mdfn/contentfn` — explicit Markdown content-type bridge
* `@mdfn/searchfn` — indexing and extraction bridge
* `@mdfn/ai` — provider-neutral assistant actions expressed as reviewable transactions or suggestions

Extension packs should use subpath exports rather than one workspace package per node or mark.

## Dependency policy

Allowed dependencies flow downward only:

* Markdown may depend on core types that are environment-neutral.
* Render may depend on core and Markdown.
* DOM and source may depend on core, Markdown, and render.
* Adapter kit may depend on environment-neutral core APIs.
* Framework packages may depend on adapter kit and browser layers.
* Components may depend on core contracts and UIFn recipes, with framework component packages depending on their matching adapters.
* Optional integrations may depend on stable foundation packages and the relevant Superfunctions package.
* Core must never import DOM, framework, UIFn, product integration, collaboration, or server packages.

A repository verifier must fail forbidden edges, framework cross-imports, private deep imports, circular dependencies, missing package metadata, or public exports that bypass the declared graph.

## Document and snapshot model

```ts
interface MdfnSnapshot {
  format: "mdfn";
  version: 1;
  markdown: string;
  document?: MdfnJSON;
  schemaHash: string;
  sourceHash: string;
  diagnostics: Diagnostic[];
  sidecar?: MdfnSidecar;
}

interface MdfnSidecar {
  comments?: CommentThread[];
  suggestions?: Suggestion[];
  assets?: AssetMetadata[];
  historyRef?: string;
}

interface MdfnJSON {
  type: "doc";
  schemaVersion: number;
  attrs?: Record<string, unknown>;
  content: MdfnNode[];
}

interface MdfnNode {
  type: string;
  attrs?: Record<string, unknown>;
  marks?: MdfnMark[];
  content?: MdfnNode[];
  text?: string;
  source?: {
    from: number;
    to: number;
    raw?: string;
    syntax?: Record<string, unknown>;
    preservation: "exact" | "semantic" | "opaque";
  };
}
```

Stable node identifiers are required where comments, suggestions, collaborative anchors, or external references need identity. Identifiers must not leak into portable Markdown unless a syntax extension explicitly owns them.

## Parse, edit, and serialize pipeline

 1. Detect dialect, extension configuration, encoding, and line endings.
 2. Parse to a positional Markdown AST with raw slices for relevant constructs.
 3. Resolve syntax through the enabled extension registry.
 4. Convert supported nodes into the runtime document.
 5. Preserve unsupported or disabled syntax as opaque nodes with diagnostics.
 6. Record source spans and formatting metadata needed by the declared preservation level.
 7. Apply edits through transactions and schema validation.
 8. Track dirty spans and structural dependencies.
 9. Serialize unchanged regions from source slices when exact preservation applies.
10. Serialize edited regions through extension serializers.
11. Format only when explicitly requested or when an edit requires local normalization.
12. Emit diagnostics for lossy conversions, unsupported constructs, invalid nesting, security policy decisions, and migration needs.

## Core transaction contract

The core engine needs:

* Immutable or persistence-friendly document state
* Selections and positions
* Atomic steps and invertible transactions
* Command dispatch and command capability checks
* History grouping and undo/redo
* Schema validation
* Plugin state
* Append/filter transaction hooks
* Mapping positions through edits
* Deterministic JSON serialization
* Extension-controlled migrations
* Diagnostic accumulation
* Stable semantic traces for testing

Consumers should receive explicit change objects including document changes, selection changes, changed source spans, diagnostics, and sidecar anchor mappings.

## Extension SDK

Each extension may contribute:

```ts
interface MdfnExtension {
  name: string;
  version: string;
  priority?: number;
  schema?: SchemaContribution;
  parseMarkdown?: MarkdownParseRules;
  serializeMarkdown?: MarkdownSerializeRules;
  render?: RenderRules;
  sanitize?: SecurityPolicyContribution;
  commands?: CommandMap;
  keymap?: KeyBinding[];
  inputRules?: InputRule[];
  pasteRules?: PasteRule[];
  plugins?: CorePlugin[];
  migrations?: SchemaMigration[];
  domRenderers?: Record<string, DomRenderer>;
  diagnostics?: DiagnosticRule[];
  tests?: ExtensionConformanceManifest;
  preservation?: PreservationDeclaration;
}
```

Extensions must declare syntax ownership, conflicts, dependencies, preservation behavior, security behavior, and migration compatibility. The registry rejects incompatible extension graphs before editor creation.

## Dialect and extension strategy

* Baseline: CommonMark
* Default: GFM
* Candidate extension packs: frontmatter, footnotes, math, callouts, directives, diagrams, custom fenced blocks, mentions, assets
* Raw HTML: opt-in policy extension, disabled by default
* Executable mixed-framework syntax: separate opt-in family with isolated parsing, rendering, and security contracts

Each extension requires parser, serializer, renderer, diagnostics, migration, unknown-syntax, security, and round-trip fixtures.

## Browser editing layer

The DOM layer is responsible for:

* Browser selection synchronization
* Before-input and input handling
* Composition and IME safety
* Clipboard import/export
* Drag/drop
* Focus and blur
* DOM mutation reconciliation
* Node views and decorators
* Scrolling and coordinate mapping
* Accessibility semantics
* Mobile behavior
* Browser-specific compatibility

Browser primitives should come from a proven structured-editing kernel. mdfn owns the surrounding contracts, Markdown fidelity, extensions, tests, and public API.

## Source editing and mode synchronization

Source mode should use a dedicated source-editor engine behind `@mdfn/source`. The integration must:

* Share the same Markdown diagnostics and extension registry
* Map selections between source and structured views where possible
* Preserve scroll and active heading context
* Debounce parsing without losing deterministic state
* Surface syntax errors without destroying the last valid structured state
* Define whether split mode updates continuously or transactionally
* Handle edits that cannot be represented by the active structured schema
* Keep undo behavior intelligible when switching modes

The source is authoritative at persistence boundaries. Visual edits update source through the preservation-aware serializer.

## Framework contract

The vanilla DOM API is the browser reference surface. Framework adapters provide:

* Editor lifecycle creation and disposal
* Fine-grained state subscriptions
* Stable action and command bindings
* Node-view rendering bridges
* Portal/overlay integration
* SSR-safe imports and hydration boundaries
* Framework-native context and composition APIs

They must not implement unique command logic, normalization, parsing, serialization, schema, or persistence behavior.

A shared semantic trace describes inputs and expected transactions, document output, selection, diagnostics, and emitted events. The same trace runs against vanilla DOM, React, Svelte, and Solid.

## UIFn integration

mdfn components should consume UIFn foundations for:

* Buttons and toggles
* Tooltips
* Menus and command palettes
* Dialogs and popovers
* Focus scopes and roving focus
* Tabs and mode switching
* Forms and comboboxes
* Theming and tokens
* Responsive layout
* Screen-reader semantics

UIFn components dispatch mdfn commands and read mdfn state. They never mutate document structure directly.

## Rendering and security

The render pipeline must support browser and server output with:

* Escaping by default
* URL protocol allowlists
* Link target and rel policies
* Raw HTML gating and sanitization
* Image and asset policies
* Embed allowlists and sandbox attributes
* Extension-specific sanitizers
* Maximum nesting, node, token, and input-size limits
* Time and memory budgets
* Safe diagnostic output
* Trusted-types compatibility where applicable

Pasted HTML follows a separate import policy and is normalized through schema-aware rules. It must never bypass render sanitization.

Security verification includes malicious Markdown corpora, unsafe URLs, malformed Unicode, deep nesting, large tokens, parser differentials, paste payloads, embed policies, authorization checks, and fuzzing.

## Collaboration architecture

The collaboration package wraps a proven shared-document engine behind mdfn contracts:

* Document update encoding
* Awareness and presence
* Selection anchors
* Offline queueing and reconnect
* Snapshot compaction
* Schema version negotiation
* Migration coordination
* Comment and suggestion anchors
* Authorization callbacks
* Audit events

The core remains usable without collaboration dependencies. Comments and suggestions live in sidecar state and map through document transactions. Conflict-safe migration requires a protocol that prevents incompatible clients from editing the same document version.

## Server architecture

`@mdfn/server` should expose services and transport-neutral handlers for:

* Document create/read/update/version operations
* Snapshot and update persistence
* Collaboration sessions
* Comment and suggestion workflows
* Asset authorization and metadata
* History and restore
* Schema/version negotiation
* Health and diagnostics

HTTP adapters remain consumer-selected. The package uses shared HTTP router contracts and does not re-export framework adapters.

Incoming shared database adapters are wrapped internally:

```ts
const database = wrapWithSchema(config.database, getMdfnSchema(config));
```

Consumers should not have to pass an mdfn schema into shared database adapter constructors.

## Superfunctions integration contracts

### DocsFn adoption

* Replace duplicated Markdown interpretation with `@mdfn/markdown`.
* Supply a DocsFn extension bundle.
* Project the canonical AST/document into current DocsFn blocks during migration.
* Run compatibility fixtures before switching defaults.
* Preserve existing rendering output or document intentional migrations.

### ContentFn adoption

* Add an explicit Markdown content type and version.
* Preserve current rich-text blocks as a separate format.
* Provide opt-in conversions with diagnostics for loss.
* Store extension and raw-HTML policies with content metadata.

### CmsFn adoption

* Compose mdfn editor components in its authoring application.
* Persist through explicit ContentFn Markdown values or mdfn snapshots.
* Supply migration tooling and previews for existing rich text.

### FileFn adoption

Define an asset provider:

```ts
interface MdfnAssetProvider {
  select?(context: AssetContext): Promise<AssetReference>;
  upload?(file: File, context: AssetContext): Promise<AssetReference>;
  resolve(reference: AssetReference): Promise<ResolvedAsset>;
  authorize?(operation: AssetOperation, reference: AssetReference): Promise<void>;
}
```

Source should prefer durable identifiers or stable references; renderers resolve delivery URLs.

### SearchFn adoption

Expose deterministic extraction:

* `extractPlainText`
* `extractHeadings`
* `extractLinks`
* `extractChunks`
* `extractMetadata`

All functions accept the same dialect and extension configuration as the editor.

## Delivery phases

### Phase 0 — Contracts and risk spikes

Deliver:

* Product scope and non-goals
* Source-preservation specification
* Runtime document and snapshot specification
* Package DAG and dependency rules
* Extension SDK contract
* Dialect and security policy
* Framework parity contract
* Editing-kernel and source-editor evaluation
* Collaboration-engine evaluation
* Representative syntax and browser risk prototypes

Exit criteria:

* Exact, semantic, and opaque preservation behaviors pass representative fixtures.
* Unknown syntax survives a no-edit cycle.
* Transactions can map source spans.
* One custom extension parses, edits, serializes, renders, diagnoses, and migrates.
* Vanilla DOM plus one framework spike demonstrates shared semantics.
* Licensing, bundle, SSR, IME, mobile, and browser constraints are understood.

### Phase 1 — Headless foundation

Deliver:

* `@mdfn/core`
* `@mdfn/markdown`
* `@mdfn/render`
* Initial extension packs
* Snapshot and migration model
* Diagnostics and formatter
* Headless testing package
* Safe read-only rendering

Exit criteria:

* CommonMark/GFM corpus gates pass.
* Supported syntax meets semantic round-trip thresholds.
* No-edit fixtures meet exact-preservation targets.
* Unknown constructs remain opaque with diagnostics.
* Security corpus and parser fuzz harness are active.
* Packages work in isolated packed consumers.

### Phase 2 — Browser editing

Deliver:

* `@mdfn/dom`
* `@mdfn/source`
* Visual, source, split, preview, and read-only modes
* History, commands, selection, clipboard, drag/drop, composition
* Essential node views
* Browser and mobile harnesses

Exit criteria:

* Editing semantics pass Chrome, Firefox, and Safari matrices.
* IME/composition suites cover representative input methods.
* Clipboard fixtures cover internal, Markdown, HTML, office-like, and plain-text sources.
* Source/visual switching preserves document and selection expectations.
* Keystroke, parse, and memory budgets pass representative large documents.
* SSR imports are side-effect safe.

### Phase 3 — Framework adapters and UI

Deliver:

* Adapter kit
* React, Svelte, and Solid packages
* Headless and styled editor components
* UIFn-based toolbar, bubble controls, command palette, links, tables, files, outline, diagnostics
* Registry composition
* Framework examples and packed consumers

Exit criteria:

* Every semantic trace passes for vanilla DOM, React, Svelte, and Solid.
* No framework package owns unique editor semantics.
* Accessibility checks cover keyboard navigation, screen readers, focus, dialogs, and high contrast.
* SSR/hydration examples pass for supported framework environments.
* Package graph verifier passes with zero forbidden edges.

### Phase 4 — Ecosystem adoption

Deliver:

* DocsFn canonical parser integration and compatibility projection
* Explicit ContentFn Markdown type
* CmsFn authoring integration
* FileFn asset provider
* SearchFn extraction bridge
* Migration and compatibility tooling

Exit criteria:

* Existing DocsFn fixtures pass or have approved documented migrations.
* ContentFn storage remains explicit and versioned.
* CmsFn can author, preview, save, reload, and migrate Markdown content.
* File references survive save/reload and authorization changes.
* Search output matches canonical document interpretation.
* Downstream packages consume public APIs only.

### Phase 5 — Collaboration and editorial platform

Deliver:

* Collaboration provider contracts and implementation
* Client/server packages
* Presence and offline synchronization
* Comments, suggestions, review state, and history
* AuthFn/HTTP/database integrations
* Operational diagnostics and compaction

Exit criteria:

* Concurrent and offline edit simulations converge.
* Anchors survive representative edits and migrations.
* Incompatible schemas are negotiated or rejected safely.
* Authorization and audit tests cover document, comment, suggestion, asset, and history operations.
* Persistence recovery and compaction tests pass.
* Multi-user performance budgets pass.

## Verification matrix

### Parser and serializer

* CommonMark corpus
* GFM corpus
* Extension fixtures
* No-edit byte identity
* Semantic round trips
* Touched-region normalization
* Unknown and disabled syntax
* Line endings and Unicode
* Malformed and adversarial input
* Migration chains

### Core engine

* Transaction invertibility
* Position mapping
* Selection mapping
* History grouping
* Command availability
* Plugin isolation
* Schema validation
* Diagnostics
* Deterministic snapshots
* Sidecar anchor mapping

### Browser

* Chrome, Firefox, Safari
* Desktop and mobile viewports
* Keyboard-only operation
* IME and composition
* Screen readers
* Clipboard sources
* Drag/drop
* Focus and overlays
* Large documents
* DOM mutation recovery

### Frameworks

* Vanilla reference traces
* React traces and SSR
* Svelte traces and SSR
* Solid traces and SSR
* Node-view lifecycle
* Subscription cleanup
* Hydration boundaries
* Framework package isolation

### Security

* Raw HTML policy
* URL sanitization
* Paste sanitization
* Embed sandboxing
* Asset authorization
* Resource exhaustion
* Fuzzing
* Collaboration authorization
* Snapshot validation
* Extension policy conflicts

### Packaging

* ESM consumers
* CommonJS consumers where promised
* Type declarations
* Tree shaking
* Side-effect declarations
* Browser/server entry separation
* Export maps
* Packed installs
* Workspace-boundary verifier
* Minimum supported runtimes

## Performance budgets to define in Phase 0

Set explicit budgets for:

* Initial parse by document size
* Incremental edit and keystroke latency
* Markdown serialization latency
* Source/visual mode switch latency
* Memory by document size
* DOM nodes and viewport rendering
* Clipboard import latency
* Collaboration update size and fan-out
* Snapshot load and compaction
* Server render throughput

Budgets should be validated on representative documents, lower-powered devices, and all supported browsers.

## Repository placement

Create mdfn as a top-level multi-package function inside the root monorepo, not a nested monorepo.

Recommended planning bundle:

```text
mdfn/
  .conduct/
    MDFN-01/
      product.md
      content-model.md
      architecture.md
      extension-sdk.md
      security.md
      verification.md
      phases.md
```

Published function packages follow the multi-package form `@mdfn/<package>`, with the curated facade published as `mdfn`. Shared ecosystem-independent primitives belong in `packages/` only if multiple functions genuinely own the abstraction.

## Engineering effort and team shape

Engineering-effort bands:

* Contracts and risk spikes: **4–6 engineer-weeks**
* Integrated prototype: **8–12 engineer-weeks**
* Production headless/browser foundation: **9–15 engineer-months**
* Complete self-hosted platform: **18–30 engineer-months**

A practical team shape includes:

* Editing/browser architecture ownership
* Markdown/parser and source-fidelity ownership
* Cross-framework and UIFn ownership
* Collaboration/backend ownership when Phase 5 begins
* Dedicated accessibility and security review capacity

Do not convert these bands into calendar commitments until Phase 0 closes the kernel, preservation, syntax, browser, and collaboration risks.

## Immediate next decision

Before implementation, approve or revise:

 1. The three-level preservation contract
 2. CommonMark baseline and GFM default
 3. Stable versus optional package boundary
 4. Extension SDK responsibilities
 5. Framework parity contract
 6. Raw HTML and embed security defaults
 7. First stable release boundary
 8. DocsFn compatibility approach
 9. ContentFn/CmsFn migration approach
10. Editing-kernel and collaboration-engine spike criteria

## Definition of ready for implementation

The work is ready to enter implementation only when:

* Product scope and non-goals are approved.
* Preservation behavior is specified per syntax class.
* Public packages and dependency rules are approved.
* Extension conflicts and migrations are specified.
* Security defaults are explicit.
* Representative risk spikes pass.
* Corpus and semantic trace fixtures exist.
* Performance budgets are set.
* Ecosystem compatibility owners accept their integration contracts.
* Each delivery phase has executable verification and rollback criteria.

## Backlog boundary

This document is a delivery plan, not an authorization to implement. [SFN-20](<https://linear.app/21n/issue/SFN-20/build-mdfn-as-the-superfunctions-markdown-authoring-platform>) remains unassigned, unscheduled, and in the SF Next backlog until it is explicitly prioritized."
  }
}

    96	  for (const extension of ordered) {
    97	    for (const [name, command] of Object.entries(extension.commands ?? {})) {
    98	      const qualified = `${extension.name}:${name}`;
    99	      if (commands[qualified]) {
   100	        throw new ExtensionGraphError("MDFN_EXTENSION_COMMAND_DUPLICATE", `Duplicate command: ${qualified}`, extension.name);
   101	      }
   102	      commands[qualified] = command;
   103	    }
   104	  }
   105	
   106	  const schemaHash = hashValue(
   107	    ordered.map((extension) => ({
   108	      name: extension.name,
   109	      version: extension.version,
   110	      schema: extension.schema ?? null,
   111	      preservation: extension.preservation,
   112	      security: extension.security ?? null,
   113	    })),
   114	  );
   115	
   116	  return {
   117	    extensions: ordered,
   118	    schemaHash,
   119	    commands,
   120	    diagnose(document) {
   121	      return ordered.flatMap((extension) => extension.diagnostics?.(document) ?? []);
   122	    },
   123	    migrate(document, fromVersion, toVersion) {
   124	      if (fromVersion === toVersion) return document;
   125	      if (fromVersion > toVersion) {
   126	        throw new ExtensionGraphError("MDFN_SCHEMA_DOWNGRADE_FORBIDDEN", "Schema downgrades are not supported");
   127	      }
   128	      let current = document;
   129	      let version = fromVersion;
   130	      while (version < toVersion) {
   131	        const migrations = ordered
   132	          .flatMap((extension) => extension.migrations ?? [])
   133	          .filter((migration) => migration.from === version)
   134	          .sort((a, b) => a.to - b.to);
   135	        const next = migrations.find((migration) => migration.to <= toVersion);
   136	        if (!next) {
   137	          throw new ExtensionGraphError(
   138	            "MDFN_SCHEMA_MIGRATION_MISSING",
   139	            `No schema migration from version ${version} to ${toVersion}`,
   140	          );
   141	        }
   142	        current = next.migrate(current);
   143	        version = next.to;
   144	      }
   145	      return current;
   146	    },
   147	  };

     1	# mdfn
     2	
     3	mdfn is the Markdown-native authoring platform for Superfunctions. Markdown is
     4	the durable boundary; structured editor state is derived, versioned, and
     5	replaceable.
     6	
     7	The package graph separates environment-neutral parsing, transactions, safe
     8	rendering, and extension contracts from browser editing, framework bindings,
     9	UIFn chrome, persistence, collaboration, and ecosystem bridges.
    10	
    11	## Guarantees
    12	
    13	- No-edit import/export is byte-identical.
    14	- Supported syntax has a semantic round trip.
    15	- Visual edits normalize only the touched top-level source regions whenever
    16	  their source spans remain mappable.
    17	- Unsupported and disabled constructs survive as opaque nodes with
    18	  diagnostics.
    19	- Raw HTML is disabled by default.
    20	- React, Svelte, Solid, and vanilla DOM share the same semantic controller.
    21	- Comments, suggestions, review transitions, history, and audit data live in a
    22	  validated sidecar bound to the canonical source.
    23	- Collaboration updates are authenticated before application and must match
    24	  the document, schema, profile, protocol, and extension contract.
    25	- Durable server operation is transactional; the explicit ephemeral mode is
    26	  reserved for memory-backed tests and examples.
    27	
    28	## Authoring surfaces
    29	
    30	`@mdfn/components` exposes the framework-neutral toolbar, slash-command,
    31	outline, diagnostics, asset, and editorial models. The React, Svelte, and Solid
    32	component packages render the same model with UIFn. The vanilla DOM adapter and
    33	all framework adapters share command, selection, undo/redo, file-drop, paste,
    34	and source-fallback semantics.
    35	
    36	Framework packages publish separate browser and server entry points. Packed
    37	consumer verification builds and executes browser and SSR applications for all
    38	three framework adapters and checks ESM, CJS, and extension subpath exports.
    39	
    40	## Verification
    41	
    42	From the repository root:
    43	
    44	```sh
    45	npm run verify:mdfn
    46	npm run verify:mdfn-browser
    47	npm run verify:mdfn-consumers
    48	```
    49	
    50	The complete gate includes the official CommonMark examples, deterministic
    51	fuzz and large-document checks, package builds/typechecks/tests/packs, runtime
    52	export checks, SSR execution, and Chromium, Firefox, WebKit, and mobile browser
    53	flows.
    54	
    55	See `mdfn/.conduct/MDFN-01` for the normative product, content, architecture,
    56	extension, security, verification, and delivery contracts.

     5	## Purpose
     6	
     7	mdfn is Superfunctions' Markdown-native authoring platform. Markdown is the durable, portable, reviewable, and version-control-friendly source of truth.     10	
    11	- Library authors use the headless controller, parser, serializer, renderer, and extension contract.
    12	- Application authors use DOM and source surfaces, framework lifecycle adapters, and UIFn-owned components.

    17

    19	
    20	## Non-negotiable guarantees
    21	
    22	1. A parse followed by serialization with no edits returns the exact input bytes.
    23	2. Supported edited syntax round-trips semantically.
    24	3. A visual edit normalizes the smallest safely mappable top-level source region.
    25	4. Unsupported syntax is preserved as opaque source with diagnostics.
    26	5. Raw HTML is disabled unless a host opts in and supplies sanitation.

     1	# MDFN-01 Content Model
     2	
     3	## Canonical boundary
     4	
     5	The canonical value is UTF-8 Markdown source plus a versioned sidecar. The source hash, extension schema hash, diagnostics, and optional projected document form an exportable snapshot. Selection and transient view state are not canonical content.
     6	
     7	## Document model
     8	
     9	`MdfnDocument` is a typed tree rooted at `doc`. Nodes carry a type, optional stable identifier, attributes, marks, children or text, and an optional `SourceSpan`. A source span stores UTF-16 offsets, raw source, syntax metadata, a preservation level, and dirty state.
    10	
    11	The baseline is CommonMark. GFM tables, task lists, strikethrough, and autolinks are enabled by the default profile. Extension nodes share the same tree and preservation protocol.
    12	
    13	## Preservation levels
    14	
    15	- Exact: untouched source is returned byte-for-byte, including whitespace, line endings, fence choices, and equivalent syntax choices.
    16	- Semantic: supported edited content retains meaning while the touched region may normalize.
    17	- Opaque: unsupported or disabled constructs retain raw source and remain uneditable until an extension owns them.
    18	
    19	The serializer first returns the original source for a clean document, then attempts descending-offset top-level region patches for dirty nodes, and only performs whole-document semantic serialization when source mapping is no longer sound. Every fallback emits a diagnostic.
    20	
    21	## Sidecar
    22	
    23	Comments, suggestions, asset metadata, and a history reference live in `MdfnSidecar`. Anchors are source ranges mapped through every transaction. Accepted edits update source; rejected suggestions stay as history until removed. Collaboration synchronizes source and sidecar through the same controller boundary.
    24	
    25	## Snapshots and migrations
    26	
    27	Snapshots are versioned, source-hashed, and schema-hashed. A matching extension schema may restore the projected document directly. A mismatch reparses canonical source and allows registered extension migrations to advance schema versions deterministically.
    28	
    29	## Limits
    30	
    31	Parsers and renderers enforce bytes, token length, node count, tree depth, output size, and URL policy limits. Limit failures are explicit and never produce partial authoritative content.

     1	# MDFN-01 Architecture
     2	
     3	Status: Approved architecture freeze for SFN-20.
     4	
     5	## Layering
     6	
     7	1. Core: immutable state, transactions, commands, history, snapshots, anchors, extension resolution.
     8	2. Markdown and render: canonical syntax projection, preservation-aware serialization, secure HTML/render tree, deterministic extraction.
     9	3. Browser: ProseMirror visual projection and CodeMirror source projection, both controlled by the same core state.
    10	4. Adapters: shared adapter-kit plus isolated React, Svelte, and Solid lifecycles.
    11	5. Components: framework-neutral toolbar model rendered only with matching UIFn framework packages.
    12	6. Platform: Yjs collaboration, typed client, and adapter-neutral self-hosted server.
    13	7. Bridges: assets, explicit content typing, search extraction, and validated AI edits.
    14	
    15	`mdfn/package-graph.json` is executable architecture. Stable packages cannot depend on optional packages, framework packages cannot import another framework, and environment-neutral packages cannot import browser/framework/Node-only runtimes.
    16	
    17	## Controller protocol
    18	
    19	All changes are immutable transactions. Source replacements reparse canonical Markdown, map sidecar anchors, update hashes and diagnostics, and enter history. Structural visual changes serialize through the projector. Selection-only transactions do not enter document history. Adapters subscribe to versioned snapshots and expose real undo/redo capability.
    20	
    21	## Visual projection
    22	
    23	The DOM package maps mdfn nodes to a ProseMirror schema. Source span attributes survive on top-level projected blocks. Comparing the previous and current ProseMirror document marks only changed blocks dirty before canonical serialization. Tables, lists, history, keymaps, paste policy, gap/drop cursors, and core commands are actual ProseMirror plugins and commands.
    24	
    25	## Source projection
    26	
    27	The source package creates a CodeMirror 6 state/view with Markdown language support, history, search, lint diagnostics, and controller synchronization. Local source edits dispatch the smallest changed range; external controller edits replace CodeMirror content without feedback loops.
    28	
    29	## Server
    30	
    31	The server wraps the incoming `@superfunctions/db` adapter with its own schema. It validates canonical Markdown, stores source/schema hashes and sidecar data, uses expected versions for optimistic concurrency, writes immutable revisions, records idempotency receipts, persists collaboration updates, and authorizes every action. Its Web Standard router is consumable through existing HTTP adapters without re-exporting them.
    32	
    33	## Risk decisions
    34	
    35	- Kernel replacement is considered only if independent preservation, transaction, history, and adapter-parity probes cannot meet the contract.
    36	- Source engine replacement is considered only if CodeMirror cannot preserve large-document editing, diagnostics, and synchronization performance.
    37	- Collaboration replacement is considered only if Yjs state vectors, offline updates, awareness, and schema negotiation fail production probes.

     1	# MDFN-01 Extension Contract
     2	
     3	Extensions declare a unique name/version, preservation behavior, dependencies/conflicts, optional schema nodes and marks, Markdown parse/serialize hooks, secure render hooks, commands, keymaps, input/paste rules, diagnostics, migrations, and security capabilities.
     4	
     5	Resolution is deterministic by dependency order, priority, and name. Duplicate names, missing dependencies, cycles, declared conflicts, duplicate commands, duplicate keymaps, and executable-content claims are hard errors. The resolved registry produces a stable schema hash.
     6	
     7	## Lifecycle
     8	
     9	1. Parse hooks claim source only from a current UTF-16 offset and report consumed length.
    10	2. Claimed source is masked for the baseline parser while line endings and offsets remain stable.
    11	3. The node receives exact raw source and the extension's preservation declaration.
    12	4. Serialize hooks own only their node type. Returning `null` delegates to built-in or opaque handling.
    13	5. Render hooks must return inert HTML and pass through the renderer's output/URL limits.
    14	6. Diagnostic hooks inspect the final document.
    15	7. Migrations are explicit adjacent schema-version transitions.
    16	
    17	## Certification
    18	
    19	`@mdfn/testing` certifies no-edit preservation, edited serialization, render output, diagnostics, and migrations. A registry recipe is publishable only when dependency/security resolution and certification pass. The callout/diagram implementations are reference extensions and their tests cover the full lifecycle.
    20	
    21	## Security
    22	
    23	Extensions cannot execute embedded content. Raw HTML capability is separately declared and still requires a host sanitizer. URL schemes are allowlisted. Extension names and conflicts are host-controlled, not source-controlled.

     1	# MDFN-01 Security Contract
     2	
     3	Raw HTML is disabled by default and preserved as an opaque node. Opt-in rendering requires a host-provided sanitizer; no package ships an implicit bypass. The renderer escapes text/attributes, blocks dangerous schemes, allows only explicit URL schemes, adds safe external-link relations, and enforces output/node/depth limits.
     4	
     5	Paste enters through the DOM package policy before ProseMirror interprets it. Source parsing has byte, token, node, and depth limits. Rendering has output limits. Server writes reparse source and reject invalid/oversized input before persistence.
     6	
     7	Collaboration updates may pass through an async authorization hook. A document stores its schema hash in shared metadata; mismatched cl…780 tokens truncated…gate. `npm run verify:mdfn` performs per-package typecheck, test, build, packed-file, packed-consumer, SSR, and browser verification. `npm run verify:mdfn-consumers` and `npm run verify:mdfn-browser` run the two environment gates independently. The completion report records exact commands, outputs, and any environment-only gap.
    23	
    24	## Failure policy
    25	
    26	No warning is relabeled as a pass. A failed required command blocks completion unless evidence shows an unrelated pre-existing repository failure; that distinction is recorded with the smallest reproducer. Browser, registry, deployment, or remote CI claims require their own evidence and are not inferred from local builds.

     1	# MDFN-01 Delivery Contract
     2	
     3	## Packages
     4	
     5	The stable graph contains core, markdown, render, extensions, DOM, source, adapter-kit, three framework adapters, neutral/framework components, testing, registry, and facade packages. Optional packages contain collaboration, client/server, and ecosystem bridges. Every public package declares exports, types, files, license, engine range, repository directory, publish access, layer/status metadata, build/test/typecheck/prepack scripts, and exact internal dependencies.
     6	
     7	## Compatibility and versioning
     8	
     9	The source snapshot format and extension schema are versioned independently of npm packages. Minor releases may add node types behind extensions or additive API fields. Changes to canonical serialization, transaction meaning, snapshot format, or extension hooks require a migration and a major release. Framework peer ranges are explicit.
    10	
    11	## Publication
    12	
    13	Publication is dependency-safe: neutral foundation before browser, adapters, components, facade, and optional packages. Release inventory rows are mandatory. Packed artifacts must install without monorepo-only paths, undeclared dependencies, or cross-framework imports.
    14	
    15	## Ecosystem rollout
    16	
    17	DocsFn uses mdfn as its canonical syntax pass while retaining documentation-specific render-model projection. ContentFn adds an explicit `markdown` field kind and validates it with the mdfn parser. CmsFn Studio selects the mdfn editor for that kind. SearchFn consumes deterministic render extraction. Existing rich-text data remains supported; migration is opt-in and source-preserving.
    18	
    19	## Governance
    20	
    21	The approved contracts in this directory are normative. `package-graph.json` and verification scripts enforce the machine-checkable subset. Product behavior changes update the contract, fixtures, and gates in the same change.

     2	
     3	## Required gates
     4	
     5	- Package graph: exact internal edges, stable/optional boundary, no cycles, framework isolation, neutral-runtime isolation, release inventory.
     6	- Type/build/test: every package typechecks, builds, and runs its tests independently.

    10	- Lifecycle: subscriptions, DOM views, awareness, and fallback editors clean up exactly once.
    11	- Packaging: `npm pack --dry-run --json` for every public package and isolated consumer installs for stable facade/framework packages.
    12	- Runtime exports and SSR: packed React, Svelte, and Solid consumers must load their published ESM/CJS contracts, resolve every certified extension subpath, complete production and SSR builds, and execute the SSR output.
    13	- Browser behavior: Chromium, Firefox, WebKit, and mobile Chromium must cover keyboard editing, the shared paste policy, composition, file drop, accessibility semantics, actual mounted adapter parity, and cleanup.

    17

The budget is intentionally environment-tolerant; release tracking records finer parse, edit, and render percentiles before changing it.
    19

    21

The completion report records exact commands, outputs, and any environment-only gap.
    23	
    24	## Failure policy
    25	
    26	No warning is relabeled as a pass. A failed required command blocks completion unless evidence shows an unrelated pre-existing repository failure; that distinction is recorded with the smallest reproducer. Browser, registry, deployment, or remote CI claims require their own evidence and are not inferred from local builds.
     1	# MDFN-01 Security Contract
     2	
     3	Raw HTML is disabled by default and preserved as an opaque node. Opt-in rendering requires a host-provided sanitizer; no package ships an implicit bypass. The renderer escapes text/attributes, blocks dangerous schemes, allows only explicit URL schemes, adds safe external-link relations, and enforces output/node/depth limits.
     4	
     5	Paste enters through the DOM package policy before ProseMirror interprets it. Source parsing has byte, token, node, and depth limits. Rendering has output limits. Server writes reparse source and reject invalid/oversized input before persistence.
