{"id":"7251dcb9-16f8-4502-85d7-78d8f70f38ea","title":"SFN-20 mdfn Worktree Re-audit — 2026-08-13","content":"# <issue id="61f0b779-b4d0-4d28-a34f-ca9bf99ec43c" href="https://linear.app/21n/issue/SFN-20/build-mdfn-as-the-superfunctions-markdown-authoring-platform">SFN-20</issue> mdfn Worktree Re-audit

## Audit metadata

* **Audit date:** 2026-08-13
* **Issue:** [SFN-20 — Build mdfn as the Superfunctions Markdown authoring platform](<https://linear.app/21n/issue/SFN-20/build-mdfn-as-the-superfunctions-markdown-authoring-platform>)
* **Previous audit:** [SFN-20 mdfn Worktree Full Code Audit — 2026-08-12](<https://linear.app/21n/document/sfn-20-mdfn-worktree-full-code-audit-2026-08-12-f970c018366c>)
* **Reviewed worktree:** /Users/serro/Documents/dev/n/worktrees/superfunctions/mdfn-<issue id="61f0b779-b4d0-4d28-a34f-ca9bf99ec43c" href="https://linear.app/21n/issue/SFN-20/build-mdfn-as-the-superfunctions-markdown-authoring-platform">SFN-20</issue>
* **Reviewed branch:** codex/mdfn-<issue id="61f0b779-b4d0-4d28-a34f-ca9bf99ec43c" href="https://linear.app/21n/issue/SFN-20/build-mdfn-as-the-superfunctions-markdown-authoring-platform">SFN-20</issue>
* **Reviewed HEAD:** 97b22e9d3598d193e7021d0940e1390bf06f605a
* **Initial implementation commit:** 98f29edd5b4a6498e0d0fc4ea29ccd6faab599f9
* **Remediation commit:** 97b22e9d3598d193e7021d0940e1390bf06f605a
* **Base:** 8dddd865ee9b86571c70db87efd918152cf682fb
* **Worktree state:** clean before and after verification
* **Issue state observed during re-audit:** Done
* **Review mode:** read-only. No source, artifact, staging, commit, branch, push, publication, deployment, or Linear issue-status change was made.
* **Verdict:** **NO-GO for stable completion, publication, or ecosystem adoption**
* **New finding count:** **11 P1 / 3 P2**

## Executive summary

The remediation commit is substantial and fixes most of the concrete defects in the first audit. It adds source-bound snapshots, inert URL handling, structured extension-render output, extension-aware atomic visual blocks, transactional durability requirements, stronger collaboration contract validation, mounted adapter/browser verification, built extension subpaths, aligned runtime engines, and materially improved DocsFn/CmsFn integration.

The re-audit nevertheless finds release-blocking failures in the core promises that define <issue id="61f0b779-b4d0-4d28-a34f-ca9bf99ec43c" href="https://linear.app/21n/issue/SFN-20/build-mdfn-as-the-superfunctions-markdown-authoring-platform">SFN-20</issue>:

 1. Visual editing silently deletes unsupported inline syntax, including raw inline HTML tags and CommonMark reference links.
 2. Source mode still owns an independent CodeMirror history and never synchronizes its selection to the controller.
 3. Visual document replacements do not remap comment/suggestion anchors.
 4. Collaboration can emit unusable incremental updates without the initial Yjs state and can lose a compacted snapshot during an in-flight flush.
 5. Tenant document listing bypasses document-level authorization and returns unauthorized Markdown.
 6. Generic sidecar updates can erase or forge comments and supposedly immutable audit history.
 7. ContentFn and CmsFn still persist Markdown as a bare string instead of the explicit versioned Markdown value required by the issue.
 8. The advertised extension SDK and CommonMark/GFM release gate are materially less complete than their contracts claim.
 9. FileFn-generated asset Markdown is rejected by mdfn’s own URL policy and renders as a blocked image.
10. Framework prop-change parity, complete authoring UI behavior, and architecture enforcement remain incomplete.

The green local release command is real and useful, but it does not exercise these paths. <issue id="61f0b779-b4d0-4d28-a34f-ca9bf99ec43c" href="https://linear.app/21n/issue/SFN-20/build-mdfn-as-the-superfunctions-markdown-authoring-platform">SFN-20</issue> is currently marked Done; the evidence in this document supports reopening it and keeping publication blocked until the P1 findings are fixed and the exact release candidate is re-audited.

## Authoritative inputs and scope

The re-audit used:

* The current <issue id="61f0b779-b4d0-4d28-a34f-ca9bf99ec43c" href="https://linear.app/21n/issue/SFN-20/build-mdfn-as-the-superfunctions-markdown-authoring-platform">SFN-20</issue> issue description and acceptance criteria.
* Both canonical Linear rationale and architecture/delivery documents.
* The previous full audit and the new completion report.
* The complete base-to-HEAD change set and the remediation commit independently.
* All mdfn packages, browser/source surfaces, framework adapters, optional collaboration/server/editorial packages, UIFn component packages, and ecosystem bridges.
* Current DocsFn, ContentFn, CmsFn, FileFn, package-graph, release, consumer, browser, and test infrastructure.
* Focused executable reproductions for preservation, history/selection, sidecar mapping, collaboration, authorization, audit mutability, and asset rendering.

The completion reports were treated as implementation claims to verify, not as independent proof.

## Disposition of the previous audit

| Previous ID | Status | Re-audit assessment |
| -- | -- | -- |
| MDFN-AUD-001 | **Partial** | Disabled top-level directives/frontmatter are better preserved, but unsupported inline nodes are still dropped by the visual projection. See MDFN-REAUD-001. |
| MDFN-AUD-002 | **Closed** | Extension blocks retain identity as atomic extension_block nodes through the visual model. |
| MDFN-AUD-003 | **Closed** | Unsafe links and images are retained as inert source and blocked in DOM/render output. |
| MDFN-AUD-004 | **Closed** | Extension rendering now uses structured, policy-checked nodes rather than arbitrary HTML strings. |
| MDFN-AUD-005 | **Closed** | Snapshots carry source/document hashes and mismatches reparse canonical Markdown. |
| MDFN-AUD-006 | **Partial** | ProseMirror history was removed, but CodeMirror history still conflicts with controller history and source selection remains non-canonical. See MDFN-REAUD-002. |
| MDFN-AUD-007 | **Closed** | Incoming collaboration updates are validated against document/profile/protocol/extension metadata on an isolated candidate. |
| MDFN-AUD-008 | **Closed** | Durable mode now fails closed without transactional adapter support; ephemeral mode is explicit. |
| MDFN-AUD-009 | **Closed** | DocsFn now projects from the canonical mdfn document, retaining limited DocsFn-specific presentation parsing. |
| MDFN-AUD-010 | **Closed** | CmsFn passes dialect, raw-HTML, extension, and schema-version configuration into the widget/server validator. A separate persistence-contract gap remains; see MDFN-REAUD-008. |
| MDFN-AUD-011 | **Closed** | The browser gate now mounts real vanilla, React, Svelte, and Solid adapters. Its vector remains narrow; see MDFN-REAUD-012. |
| MDFN-AUD-012 | **Closed** | Directive closing syntax no longer consumes following blank lines. |
| MDFN-AUD-013 | **Closed** | The five extension subpaths are explicit build inputs and pass packed-consumer import checks. |
| MDFN-AUD-014 | **Closed** | Runtime engine contracts are aligned for packages that depend on mdfn at runtime. |

**Prior-audit result:** 12 closed, 2 partially closed.

## Findings overview

| ID | Priority | Area | Finding |
| -- | -- | -- | -- |
| MDFN-REAUD-001 | P1 | Preservation / visual editing | Unsupported inline nodes are silently deleted by visual edits |
| MDFN-REAUD-002 | P1 | Source mode / core | CodeMirror and the controller still maintain conflicting histories; source selection is not canonical |
| MDFN-REAUD-003 | P1 | Editorial anchors | Visual document replacement does not remap sidecar anchors |
| MDFN-REAUD-004 | P1 | Collaboration | The sendUpdate path omits initialization and can send dependency-incomplete Yjs updates |
| MDFN-REAUD-005 | P1 | Collaboration | Queue compaction during an in-flight flush can discard the replacement snapshot |
| MDFN-REAUD-006 | P1 | Authorization | Tenant listing bypasses per-document authorization and leaks content |
| MDFN-REAUD-007 | P1 | Audit / editorial integrity | Generic sidecar updates can erase or forge comments and audit history |
| MDFN-REAUD-008 | P1 | ContentFn / CmsFn | Markdown is still stored as a bare string, not a versioned profile-bound value |
| MDFN-REAUD-009 | P1 | Extension SDK | Advertised extension lifecycle capabilities are absent or inert |
| MDFN-REAUD-010 | P1 | Verification | The official CommonMark gate is a no-edit byte-retention loop, not a semantic conformance gate; no official GFM corpus is run |
| MDFN-REAUD-011 | P1 | FileFn | Generated asset Markdown is blocked by mdfn itself |
| MDFN-REAUD-012 | P2 | Adapter parity | Svelte/Solid do not react to important prop changes after async editor creation |
| MDFN-REAUD-013 | P2 | Authoring UI | Required UI surfaces are mostly always-visible/static scaffolds rather than complete workflows |
| MDFN-REAUD-014 | P2 | Architecture gate | Package-graph verification under-enforces the documented dependency/publication contract |

## Detailed findings

### MDFN-REAUD-001 — Unsupported inline nodes are silently deleted by visual edits

**Priority:** P1

**Affected code**

* mdfn/markdown/src/index.ts:146-155
* mdfn/dom/src/schema.ts:65-76
* mdfn/dom/src/schema.ts:136-143

**Evidence**

The Markdown projector represents raw HTML and unknown mdast nodes as generic opaque nodes. The DOM projection handles text, inline code, images, and hard breaks, then recursively descends into every other node. An inline opaque node has no child content, so it becomes nothing in ProseMirror.

Two independent edit-path reproductions:

* Source: before <custom-tag>inside</custom-tag> after
  * Parsed children: text, opaque, text, opaque, text
  * Visual text: before inside after
  * After inserting X visually: Xbefore inside after
  * Both raw tags were deleted.
* Source: [label][ref] followed by its [ref] definition
  * The inline linkReference parsed as opaque.
  * Visual text for the reference was empty.
  * After a visual edit the serialized paragraph became X; the link reference was deleted while the separate definition remained.

The official CommonMark corpus includes reference-link syntax, so this is not merely an exotic extension case.

**Impact**

A user can open valid or unsupported Markdown in visual mode and lose source content on the next edit. This violates the durable Markdown contract, opaque-node behavior, CommonMark baseline, source/visual equivalence, and the explicit prohibition on silently discarding unsupported constructs.

**Required remediation**

* Add an inline opaque representation to the visual schema, with exact source/identity retained.
* Implement native reference-link/reference-image support or an inert editable fallback.
* Prevent edits near unsupported inline content from forcing whole-paragraph semantic reconstruction.
* Add parse → visual edit → serialize → reparse fixtures for raw inline HTML, link/image references, footnotes, custom inline extensions, and mixed supported/unsupported marks.

### MDFN-REAUD-002 — CodeMirror and the controller still maintain conflicting histories; source selection is not canonical

**Priority:** P1

**Affected code:** mdfn/source/src/index.ts:55-101

**Evidence**

Source mode installs CodeMirror history() and historyKeymap while local source edits also dispatch into the controller, which maintains its own undo stack. The update listener only handles docChanged; it never dispatches selection-only updates.

Focused reproduction:

* Edit a → ab in CodeMirror.
* CodeMirror undo changes controller Markdown to a.
* Controller undo then changes Markdown back to ab.
* Moving the CodeMirror cursor leaves controller.getState().selection equal to null.

The remediation removed the duplicate ProseMirror history but left the same architectural conflict in source mode.

**Impact**

Undo/redo direction depends on which surface receives the command. Mode switching, collaboration transaction boundaries, toolbar state, outline navigation, comments anchored to selection, and adapter traces cannot rely on one canonical state.

**Required remediation**

* Choose one history authority across source, visual, and headless modes.
* Translate source selection into controller transactions and map controller selection back into CodeMirror.
* Specify mode-switch behavior for selection, composition, undo/redo, and remote changes.
* Add cross-mode history and selection traces, including source → visual → source and remote edits.

### MDFN-REAUD-003 — Visual document replacement does not remap sidecar anchors

**Priority:** P1

**Affected code**

* mdfn/core/src/transaction.ts:76-96
* mdfn/dom/src/index.ts:183-190

**Evidence**

replace-source operations call mapSidecar with the changed range. replace-document serializes the new document, records a full-document range, and never maps the sidecar. DOM edits dispatch replaceDocument.

Reproduction:

* Markdown: hello world
* Comment anchor: 6..11, covering world
* Visual/structural replacement: big hello world
* Resulting comment anchor remains 6..11 instead of moving to 10..15.

**Impact**

Comments and suggestions drift onto unrelated text after visual edits. Editorial decisions can then apply to the wrong source span, corrupting review integrity and creating misleading audit records.

**Required remediation**

* Derive minimal source changes from document serialization and map sidecars through those changes.
* If a precise mapping is impossible, mark the anchor orphaned/ambiguous rather than retaining a false location.
* Test insert/delete/split/join/table/list/extension edits before, within, and across anchored ranges.

### MDFN-REAUD-004 — The sendUpdate path omits initialization and can send dependency-incomplete Yjs updates

**Priority:** P1

**Affected code:** mdfn/collab/src/index.ts:94-103, 127-132, 190-201

**Evidence**

Metadata, initial Markdown, and initial sidecar are inserted before the doc update listener is registered. They are therefore absent from pendingUpdates and are never passed to sendUpdate.

Reproduction:

* Construct a session for Markdown one with sendUpdate configured.
* Immediately after construction: sent=0, pending=0.
* Edit to one!: one update is sent.
* Applying that update to an empty Y.Doc produces empty Markdown, because the incremental update depends on missing initial Yjs structs.

Tests avoid the failure by manually applying session.encodeUpdate() to each peer before exercising sendUpdate.

**Impact**

The advertised offline/reconnect transport can silently fail for a new peer unless every host implements a separate, correctly ordered bootstrap handshake. A session created offline can queue edits that are unusable without state the queue never contains.

**Required remediation**

* Make initial state synchronization an explicit enforced protocol step, or enqueue a full initial state before incremental updates.
* Prevent flush until the transport confirms the peer state vector/handshake.
* Test first peer, empty peer, offline-first document creation, reconnect without manual seeding, and persisted update replay.

### MDFN-REAUD-005 — Queue compaction during an in-flight flush can discard the replacement snapshot

**Priority:** P1

**Affected code:** mdfn/collab/src/index.ts:168-186

**Evidence**

compactPending replaces the entire pendingUpdates array with one full-state snapshot. flush captures pendingUpdates[0], awaits sendUpdate, and then calls pendingUpdates.shift() on the current array.

Reproduction with a deferred first send and a one-byte compaction threshold:

* First local update begins sending.
* Second edit compacts the queue to a new full snapshot.
* Before resolving the first send: sends=1, pending=1, local Markdown=a12.
* Resolve the first send.
* After resolution: sends=1, pending=0.
* The replacement full snapshot was shifted out without ever being sent.

**Impact**

Concurrent editing during slow network I/O loses the only update capable of converging the peer. The local queue reports empty, so the loss is silent and survives reconnect logic.

**Required remediation**

* Track queue entries by identity/generation and remove only the entry that was actually sent.
* Do not mutate/replace the active entry without preserving the replacement generation.
* Add delayed transport, concurrent edit, repeated compaction, failure/retry, offline/online race, and multi-peer convergence tests.

### MDFN-REAUD-006 — Tenant listing bypasses per-document authorization and leaks content

**Priority:** P1

**Affected code:** mdfn/server/src/index.ts:170-174 and router list response at 273

**Evidence**

list calls authorize("read", principal) once without a document, then returns every document in the tenant. Direct reads correctly call authorization with the loaded document.

Reproduction with an authorization callback that allows users to read only documents they own:

* Tenant t contains owner a document # Own and owner b document # Secret.
* service.list(principal a) returns both records, including both Markdown bodies.
* [service.read](<http://service.read>)(principal a, owner b document) fails with MDFN_FORBIDDEN.

**Impact**

Any same-tenant role policy more restrictive than “read every tenant document” is bypassed by the list endpoint. The endpoint returns titles, Markdown, sidecars, hashes, ownership, and timestamps, so this is a content disclosure rather than a metadata-only leak.

**Required remediation**

* Apply authorization to each returned document or push an authorization-safe predicate into storage.
* Define list/search pagination semantics when rows are filtered.
* Add same-tenant owner, role, ACL, draft/published, and cross-project isolation tests at service and HTTP layers.

### MDFN-REAUD-007 — Generic sidecar updates can erase or forge comments and audit history

**Priority:** P1

**Affected code**

* mdfn/server/src/index.ts:135-198
* mdfn/server/src/index.ts:281-289
* collaboration whole-sidecar replacement at mdfn/collab/src/index.ts:145-163

**Evidence**

Specialized editorial methods append structured audit entries, but the generic update method and PUT sidecar endpoint accept an arbitrary complete sidecar under the generic update permission. Validation checks shape, bounds, and anchors; it does not enforce audit immutability, actor provenance, transition legality relative to stored state, or append-only history.

Reproduction:

* createComment creates one comment and one audit entry.
* service.update with sidecar { audit: [], comments: [] } succeeds.
* Stored audit and comments both become empty.

The same replacement model is used by collaboration after candidate shape validation.

**Impact**

A client with ordinary update/collaboration permission can delete review evidence, forge actors/timestamps/actions, rewrite suggestion decisions, or bypass specialized editorial authorization. “Immutable audit entries” is therefore not a server-enforced property.

**Required remediation**

* Separate content, editorial, review, and audit permissions/actions.
* Make audit history server-authored and append-only; reject client-supplied audit replacement.
* Validate sidecar mutations against current persisted state, not only standalone shape.
* Define safe collaborative representation for editorial state and authoritative server reconciliation.
* Add tamper, privilege, replay, actor-forgery, deletion, and illegal-transition tests.

### MDFN-REAUD-008 — Markdown is still stored as a bare string, not a versioned profile-bound value

**Priority:** P1

**Affected code**

* contentfn/core/src/schema/types.ts:30-35
* contentfn/server/src/storage/docs.ts:139-151
* cmsfn/studio/src/editor/widgets/MarkdownWidget.tsx
* mdfn/contentfn/src/index.ts:3-18

**Evidence**

The ContentFn schema now carries Markdown dialect, raw-HTML, extension, and schema-version metadata. Storage validation still requires the field value itself to be typeof string. CmsFn widget value/onChange are also string-based.

In contrast, @mdfn/contentfn defines the intended MarkdownContent envelope with:

* media type and envelope version
* canonical Markdown
* complete profile
* schema hash
* optional sidecar

That envelope is not the value persisted by ContentFn/CmsFn.

**Impact**

Changing a dataset schema can silently reinterpret all existing stored strings under a different dialect, extension set, raw-HTML policy, or schema version. A document does not carry enough information to migrate, validate historically, reproduce rendering, or reject incompatible clients.

**Required remediation**

* Persist the explicit versioned MarkdownContent value or an equivalent immutable profile reference/version alongside every field value.
* Add migration for legacy strings.
* Keep schema defaults as authoring defaults, not the sole historical interpretation.
* Test schema/profile changes, old data reads, migration rollback, CmsFn editing, and API import/export.

### MDFN-REAUD-009 — Advertised extension lifecycle capabilities are absent or inert

**Priority:** P1

**Affected code**

* mdfn/core/src/types.ts:239-261
* mdfn/core/src/extensions.ts:16-147
* mdfn/.conduct/MDFN-01/extension-contract.md

**Evidence**

The issue requires schema, parsing, serialization, HTML rendering and sanitization, commands, shortcuts, input/paste rules, plugins, migrations, DOM renderers, and conformance tests.

The public interface lacks sanitizer hooks, plugin hooks, DOM editor/render hooks, and a certification manifest. keymap, inputRules, and pasteRules exist only as metadata; resolveExtensions does not expose or execute them and does not detect duplicate key bindings. inputRules/pasteRules are string arrays, not executable typed contracts. certifyExtension only runs the no-edit preservation loop. The reference extension tests do not cover the claimed full lifecycle.

**Impact**

Hosts and third-party extensions cannot implement the documented platform contract. The registry can report an extension resolved while several declared behaviors have no runtime consumer, and publication can be “certified” without edited serialization, rendering, diagnostics, migrations, visual behavior, or security checks.

**Required remediation**

* Define typed executable hooks and a single host integration path for every promised lifecycle stage.
* Resolve and conflict-check keymaps/rules/plugins.
* Add structured DOM rendering/editing hooks with opaque fallback.
* Make certification exercise edited round trips, render/security, diagnostics, migrations, visual projection, and package/runtime compatibility.

### MDFN-REAUD-010 — The official syntax gate does not establish CommonMark/GFM conformance

**Priority:** P1

**Affected code**

* mdfn/testing/src/testing.test.ts:26-30
* mdfn/testing/src/index.ts:24-43
* clean-document serialization shortcut in mdfn/markdown

**Evidence**

The 652 CommonMark examples are mapped to runPreservationCorpus. That helper parses and immediately serializes an untouched document, asserting only that the output bytes equal the original input. The serializer intentionally returns original source for a clean document, so the test can pass even when the AST semantics are wrong or unsupported.

The reference-link reproduction in MDFN-REAUD-001 demonstrates exactly this: the corpus’s no-edit check passes, but visual projection cannot represent the syntax and deletes it on edit.

There is no official GFM corpus gate. The browser gate also reports clipboardEvent=false for Firefox and WebKit; those runs validate the shared sanitizer/plaintext path but do not execute the synthetic clipboard event itself.

**Impact**

A release can claim official corpus success while failing valid syntax as soon as it is rendered or edited. The acceptance criterion calls for parser/serializer conformance and CommonMark/GFM gates, not merely a clean-source cache invariant.

**Required remediation**

* Compare parsed/rendered semantics with official expected output.
* Add supported-edit and touched-region round trips for every syntax class.
* Add an official/authoritative GFM fixture suite.
* Distinguish required browser event coverage from shared helper coverage in the release verdict.

### MDFN-REAUD-011 — FileFn-generated asset Markdown is blocked by mdfn itself

**Priority:** P1

**Affected code:** mdfn/filefn/src/index.ts:126-140 and shared URL policy/parser

**Evidence**

assetReferenceMarkdown emits image syntax using the custom mdfn-asset: scheme. The Markdown parser allows image schemes http and https only. No asset extension recognizes the custom syntax and no asynchronous resolver is connected to parsing/rendering.

Reproduction:

* Generated Markdown:

  ![asset](mdfn-asset:filefn/asset)
* Parse diagnostic: MDFN_UNSAFE_URL
* Rendered HTML: a span with data-mdfn-blocked-image=true rather than an asset.

resolvedAssetRenderNode can emit a safe resolved node, but hosts must manually bypass the Markdown path produced by assetReferenceMarkdown to use it.

**Impact**

The primary FileFn bridge output cannot round-trip into the platform as a working asset. Files inserted through the authoring UI appear blocked after reload/render, contradicting the required durable asset identity and resolver contract.

**Required remediation**

* Define an asset extension/node syntax recognized before generic URL rejection.
* Preserve durable provider/id/version identity and resolve asynchronously through an authorized gateway.
* Keep export behavior explicit for portable and platform-specific Markdown.
* Test insert → persist → reload → offline/pending → resolve → render across real FileFn authorization outcomes.

### MDFN-REAUD-012 — Svelte/Solid do not react to important prop changes after async editor creation

**Priority:** P2

**Affected code**

* mdfn/svelte/src/MdfnEditor.svelte:30-72
* mdfn/solid/src/index.tsx:42-75

**Evidence**

Both adapters synchronously track mode/targets, then read readOnly, ariaLabel, onFiles, editorRef, and load-error callbacks after dynamic-import awaits. Reactive systems do not track reads made later in an async continuation. Neither adapter has a separate setReadOnly/update effect. React includes these inputs in its lifecycle dependencies.

The parity browser vector mounts once and only performs insert/undo/redo. It never changes props or verifies attribute/callback replacement.

**Impact**

A host can toggle readOnly or change file/security callbacks and leave an existing Svelte/Solid editor using stale behavior until a mode remount. This is adapter drift in lifecycle and permission-sensitive UI behavior.

**Required remediation**

* Snapshot all lifecycle inputs synchronously or add explicit update effects.
* Use setReadOnly where a remount is unnecessary.
* Extend parity vectors with prop changes, callback replacement, controller replacement, Strict/cleanup behavior, and mode switching.

### MDFN-REAUD-013 — Required UI surfaces are mostly static scaffolds rather than complete workflows

**Priority:** P2

**Affected code:** mdfn/components-react/src/index.tsx:90-159 and equivalent generated framework components

**Evidence**

The implementation renders named surfaces, but behavior is incomplete:

* Slash menu is always visible rather than triggered/contextual.
* “Bubble” and “floating” toolbars are static duplicate toolbar regions, not selection/block-positioned controls.
* Comments can be created but not replied to or resolved in the UI.
* Suggestions can be accepted/rejected but not created in the UI.
* History renders sidecar audit entries; it does not list/restore server document versions.
* File controls depend on a host callback rather than the built FileFn gateway.
* Tests primarily assert that surfaces mount/exist, not that complete workflows function.

**Impact**

The component family satisfies surface naming more than the editor capability matrix. A product adopting it still has to build major <issue id="61f0b779-b4d0-4d28-a34f-ca9bf99ec43c" href="https://linear.app/21n/issue/SFN-20/build-mdfn-as-the-superfunctions-markdown-authoring-platform">SFN-20</issue> workflows itself.

**Required remediation**

Implement and test complete interaction workflows, responsive/keyboard behavior, positioning, version restore, editorial actions, and FileFn integration across React/Svelte/Solid parity scenarios.

### MDFN-REAUD-014 — Package-graph verification under-enforces the documented contract

**Priority:** P2

**Affected code:** scripts/verify-mdfn-package-graph.mjs:20-43

**Evidence**

The verifier checks package counts, declared internal dependency names, stable-to-optional edges, simple framework import patterns, cycles, and release rows. It does not enforce several architecture claims:

* allowed layer-to-layer dependency directions beyond stable/optional
* public/private boundary and facade rules
* deep/internal imports
* exact internal version alignment
* complete export-map target existence
* peer/dependency placement rules
* required metadata values rather than mere presence

The import regex also scans only selected source forms and can miss require, re-export, dynamic-expression, and compiled-boundary cases.

**Impact**

The graph can report ok while violating the dependency directions and package boundaries the issue calls “mechanically enforceable.”

**Required remediation**

Encode the full layer matrix and publication contract, parse imports robustly, validate export targets and internal versions, and add negative fixtures that prove every forbidden edge fails the gate.

## Verification performed

### Complete MDFN release gate

Command: npm run verify:mdfn

**Result: PASS**

Observed evidence:

* Package graph: 17 stable packages, 7 optional packages, React/Svelte/Solid framework set.
* All 24 mdfn packages built, typechecked, and ran their configured suites.
* 67 mdfn test assertions passed across the package family.
* 24/24 package dry-run packs passed.
* Isolated React/Svelte/Solid consumers passed production build, SSR build, SSR runtime, ESM/CJS runtime-export, subpath, and peer-isolation checks.
* Chromium, Firefox, WebKit, and mobile Chromium browser runs reported overall success.
* Mounted adapter parity passed the current insert/undo/redo trace.
* Worktree remained clean after the gate.

### Ecosystem regression matrix

All six affected packages built successfully:

* DocsFn core
* ContentFn core
* ContentFn server
* CmsFn core
* CmsFn server
* CmsFn Studio

Runtime suites:

* DocsFn core: 148/148 passed
* ContentFn core: 8/8 passed
* ContentFn server: 112/112 passed
* CmsFn core: 24/24 passed
* CmsFn server: 31/31 passed
* CmsFn Studio: 50/50 passed
* **Total: 373/373 assertions passed**

Typechecks:

* ContentFn core: pass
* ContentFn server: pass
* CmsFn core: pass
* CmsFn Studio: pass
* CmsFn server: fail with broad existing typing debt in tests and unrelated audit/ops/publishing/release/logging/status-client code. This re-audit does not attribute that baseline to the MDFN changes, but it means the affected ecosystem is not independently all-green.

Additional checks:

* git diff --check: pass
* clean status after all builds/tests: pass
* exact reviewed HEAD unchanged: pass

### Focused defect reproductions

The re-audit independently reproduced:

 1. Raw inline HTML tags deleted by a visual edit.
 2. A CommonMark reference link deleted by a visual edit.
 3. CodeMirror undo followed by controller undo reapplying the edit.
 4. Source cursor movement leaving controller selection null.
 5. A comment anchor failing to move after a visual document insertion.
 6. A collaboration incremental update failing on an empty peer because initialization was never sent.
 7. A compacted collaboration snapshot being dropped during an in-flight flush.
 8. Same-tenant list returning an unauthorized document that direct read forbids.
 9. Generic update deleting comment and audit history.
10. FileFn-generated asset Markdown receiving MDFN_UNSAFE_URL and rendering blocked.

## Verification qualifications

The local gates do not prove:

* Remote CI for this exact commit.
* npm registry contents or publication integrity.
* A deployed self-hosted server with a durable transactional database.
* Real authenticated multi-tenant authorization policy.
* Real multi-process/multi-device collaboration convergence and recovery.
* Production FileFn storage, signed delivery, and authorization.
* Manual screen-reader, mobile, IME, and cross-browser clipboard UX.
* Existing data migration from ContentFn/CmsFn string fields.
* Third-party extension compatibility and malicious extension behavior.

Passing builds and tests are necessary; they do not override the reproduced failures.

## Recommended remediation order

 1. **Reopen** <issue id="61f0b779-b4d0-4d28-a34f-ca9bf99ec43c" href="https://linear.app/21n/issue/SFN-20/build-mdfn-as-the-superfunctions-markdown-authoring-platform">SFN-20</issue> **and keep publication blocked.** The current Done state is inconsistent with the P1 evidence. This audit did not change issue state.
 2. **Repair the durable edit path.** Preserve inline opaque/reference nodes, map sidecars through visual edits, and add semantic official-corpus gates.
 3. **Unify source semantics.** Establish one history and selection authority across source/visual/headless modes.
 4. **Fix collaboration delivery.** Enforce bootstrap/state-vector handshakes and make queue compaction generation-safe under concurrent sends.
 5. **Close authorization and audit boundaries.** Filter lists per document and make audit/editorial transitions server-authoritative and tamper-resistant.
 6. **Adopt the content envelope.** Persist profile/version/schema identity with every ContentFn/CmsFn Markdown value and migrate legacy strings.
 7. **Make FileFn assets first-class syntax.** Connect durable asset identity, authorized resolution, and rendering through an actual extension.
 8. **Complete the extension/UI/adapter contracts.** Implement every advertised hook and workflow, then expand parity vectors beyond mount and insert/undo/redo.
 9. **Strengthen mechanical gates.** Enforce full package layering/export/version rules and distinguish semantic/browser-event coverage from helper-only coverage.
10. **Re-audit the exact release candidate.** Repeat focused negative repros as permanent regression tests and capture remote CI/publication/deployment evidence separately.

## Final assessment

The remediation commit materially improves the implementation and closes most of the first audit’s concrete defects. It is not yet the production-ready Markdown authoring platform promised by <issue id="61f0b779-b4d0-4d28-a34f-ca9bf99ec43c" href="https://linear.app/21n/issue/SFN-20/build-mdfn-as-the-superfunctions-markdown-authoring-platform">SFN-20</issue>.

The remaining failures are concentrated in durable preservation, canonical state, editorial integrity, collaboration delivery, tenant authorization, versioned content storage, extension completeness, and FileFn interoperability. These are product-defining contracts, not optional polish.

**Final verdict: NO-GO.** <issue id="61f0b779-b4d0-4d28-a34f-ca9bf99ec43c" href="https://linear.app/21n/issue/SFN-20/build-mdfn-as-the-superfunctions-markdown-authoring-platform">SFN-20</issue> **should be reopened from Done, the 11 P1 findings should block publication, and the exact fixed HEAD should be re-audited before completion is claimed again.**","icon":null,"color":"#E5484D","url":"https://linear.app/21n/document/sfn-20-mdfn-worktree-re-audit-2026-08-13-b05adb48aa62","slugId":"b05adb48aa62","createdAt":"2026-08-13T01:42:51.820Z","updatedAt":"2026-08-13T01:42:53.220Z","archivedAt":null,"creator":{"id":"3a6ed003-6380-47ef-9e7b-b2b01ebddc6a","name":"Aravind"},"updatedBy":{"id":"3a6ed003-6380-47ef-9e7b-b2b01ebddc6a","name":"Aravind"},"project":null,"initiative":null,"team":null,"issue":{"id":"SFN-20","title":"Build mdfn as the Superfunctions Markdown authoring platform"}}

{"id":"SFN-20","title":"Build mdfn as the Superfunctions Markdown authoring platform","description":"## Executive summary

Create **mdfn**, a framework-neutral Markdown authoring platform for the Superfunctions ecosystem. The product should combine a headless editing engine, first-class Markdown parsing and serialization, a vanilla DOM surface, equal framework adapters, composable editor UI built with UIFn, and optional self-hosted collaboration and platform integrations.

The durable contract is Markdown source. Runtime editor state may use a structured document model, but import, editing, export, migrations, diagnostics, and extension behavior must preserve source meaning and avoid silently discarding unsupported content.

## Problem / opportunity

Superfunctions has useful pieces for Markdown rendering, portable content blocks, file handling, search, UI, authentication, HTTP, and database access, but it does not yet have a shared authoring substrate. Existing Markdown compilation is renderer-oriented, and existing rich-text authoring surfaces do not provide a complete editing engine.

Without mdfn, each product must independently solve schema design, selection behavior, commands, history, clipboard handling, source mode, framework integration, UI parity, persistence, collaboration, and security. A shared Markdown-native platform can remove that duplication while improving interoperability across DocsFn, ContentFn, CmsFn, FileFn, SearchFn, AuthFn, and the shared HTTP/database packages.

## Expected outcome

A production-ready, self-hostable Markdown platform that supports:

* Headless document and command APIs independent of UI framework
* Canonical Markdown parsing, serialization, formatting, and diagnostics
* Visual, source, split, preview, and read-only modes
* Vanilla DOM integration plus semantically equivalent React, Svelte, and Solid adapters
* UIFn-based editor chrome without coupling editing semantics to UIFn
* Extensible schema, syntax, commands, keymaps, paste/input rules, rendering, migrations, and tests
* Optional collaboration, presence, comments, suggestions, history, assets, persistence, and AI integration
* Reuse by DocsFn, ContentFn, CmsFn, FileFn, and SearchFn through explicit compatibility contracts

## Goals

* Define the source-preservation contract before implementation.
* Support byte-identical no-edit import/export, semantic round trips for supported syntax, and touched-region normalization.
* Establish CommonMark as the baseline and GFM as the default dialect.
* Preserve unsupported constructs as diagnosable opaque nodes rather than silently dropping them.
* Provide a small stable package graph with explicit dependency directions.
* Keep the core framework-neutral, UI-neutral, storage-neutral, transport-neutral, and collaboration-neutral.
* Provide equal behavior across vanilla DOM, React, Svelte, and Solid.
* Use shared Superfunctions abstractions for HTTP, database, authentication, files, search, and UI.
* Ship conformance, parity, security, accessibility, browser, IME, clipboard, SSR, performance, migration, and packed-consumer test gates.

## Non-goals

* Building browser editing primitives, history, clipboard semantics, or collaborative merge algorithms from scratch.
* Coupling the core document model to a UI framework or component library.
* Replacing DocsFn, ContentFn, CmsFn, FileFn, SearchFn, AuthFn, or shared packages.
* Making executable mixed-framework syntax part of the default portable Markdown dialect.
* Enabling raw HTML by default.
* Creating one workspace package per document node or mark.
* Shipping implementation as part of this backlog-capture item.

## Acceptance criteria

* A reviewed product and architecture contract defines the durable Markdown model, runtime document model, source spans, syntax metadata, opaque-node behavior, diagnostics, migrations, and versioning.
* The package dependency graph and public/private package boundaries are explicit and mechanically enforceable.
* The extension SDK contract covers schema, parsing, serialization, HTML rendering and sanitization, commands, shortcuts, input and paste rules, plugins, migrations, DOM renderers, and conformance tests.
* A framework contract defines vanilla DOM behavior and adapter parity requirements for React, Svelte, and Solid.
* An editor capability matrix covers foundational editing, Markdown-native syntax, assets and embeds, UI surfaces, collaboration, persistence, import/export, and read-only rendering.
* Ecosystem integration contracts are defined for UIFn, DocsFn, ContentFn, CmsFn, FileFn, SearchFn, AuthFn, and shared HTTP/database packages.
* Security defaults and threat models cover raw HTML, links, pasted HTML, custom embeds, asset access, collaboration authorization, and denial-of-service inputs.
* Release gates cover parser and serializer conformance, round trips, unknown syntax, framework parity, browsers, mobile, IME, clipboard, SSR, accessibility, security, fuzzing, performance, packaging, migrations, and ecosystem adoption.
* The work is decomposed into independently verifiable delivery phases with explicit exit criteria.
* The two associated Linear documents remain the canonical rationale and delivery-plan references for this issue.

## Dependencies / risks

* The source-preservation guarantee constrains parser, runtime model, serializer, migrations, and collaboration design; postponing it risks irreversible architecture mistakes.
* A structured editing kernel and collaboration engine must be selected through focused risk spikes and license, bundle, SSR, browser, mobile, and IME evaluation.
* Framework adapters can drift unless all behavior is implemented in shared core and adapter layers and verified through the same semantic trace suite.
* UIFn package-boundary enforcement must be reliable before mdfn adopts the same graph-verification pattern.
* DocsFn adoption requires a compatibility projection so existing rendering behavior can migrate without a flag day.
* ContentFn and CmsFn need explicit Markdown content types and migration paths rather than silent reinterpretation of current rich-text data.
* Collaboration, comments, and suggestions require stable identifiers, schema-aware migrations, authorization hooks, auditability, and offline conflict handling.
* Untrusted Markdown, HTML, links, embeds, assets, and pasted content create security and resource-exhaustion risks.
* Package surface area can grow rapidly; stable packages must remain few, with optional capabilities and subpath exports used deliberately.

## Open questions

* Which source-preservation level is mandatory for the first stable release, and which syntax classes may normalize?
* Which structured editing kernel best satisfies the framework, browser, SSR, IME, bundle, licensing, and plugin requirements?
* Which syntax belongs in the default dialect versus opt-in extension packs?
* What is the stable public boundary between mdfn parsing/rendering and DocsFn-specific behavior?
* Should collaboration and persistence ship in the first stable platform release or follow the headless/browser foundation?
* Which content migrations are required for existing ContentFn and CmsFn data?
* What are the initial performance budgets for document size, parse latency, keystroke latency, memory, and collaboration fan-out?
* Which capabilities belong in the facade package versus explicit advanced imports?

Re-audit complete: **NO-GO — 11 P1 / 3 P2 findings.**

The main blockers are:

- Visual edits delete unsupported inline syntax, including CommonMark reference links.
- Source mode still has conflicting CodeMirror/controller histories and no canonical selection.
- Collaboration can send unusable incremental updates and lose compacted updates during concurrent flushes.
- Tenant listing bypasses document-level authorization.
- Comments and “immutable” audit history can be overwritten through generic sidecar updates.
- ContentFn/CmsFn still store unversioned Markdown strings.
- FileFn-generated asset syntax is rejected by MDFN itself.
- Extension, conformance, adapter, and authoring UI contracts remain incomplete.

The remediation closed 12 previous findings and partially closed 2. The complete MDFN gate passed, as did 373 downstream tests, but targeted negative reproductions exposed paths those gates miss. CMSFn server’s known standalone typecheck debt remains red.

The detailed audit is attached to SFN-20: [SFN-20 mdfn Worktree Re-audit — 2026-08-13](https://linear.app/21n/document/sfn-20-mdfn-worktree-re-audit-2026-08-13-b05adb48aa62).
